article.title: The Fans' View: Is this just the start for history-making Fylde?
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
With 100 points banked and 112 goals scored, AFC Fylde fans probably didn’t want their season to end. Well, that's nowhere near true of course - none of them could take another moment of a helter-skelter title race which saw the Enterprise National League North leadership change hands a couple of times every month! The final whistle blew with them sitting pretty in front of South Shields as Craig Mahon’s fantastic first season ended with promotion.

But as Coasters superfan Jack Connor tells us, if lessons can be learned from promotions past, then it could be quite the season ahead too. We’re speaking to a fan from every club this summer to get their take on the last ten months, the campaign to come and the advice they’d give to their manager if they bumped into him down the pub! What ground did you love visiting the most I would say Radcliffe.

A Tuesday night game just after Christmas and a first trip there for me. A good turnout of over 200 Coasters fans and one of the most mental games you'll have seen in the National League this season. Being 3-0 up with 25 minutes to go to almost losing the game in the 96th minute.

It felt like a defeat but I can't deny what an amazing game it was for any neutrals there that night. Who was your club’s Player of the Season? Plenty of worthy candidates but for me Tom Whelan, without a doubt.

Added that mix of quality and fight in the midfield we lacked last season and popped up with his fair share of goals as well as a bucket load of assists. Other worthy candidates include Luca Thomas and Chris Merrie. What was the single best moment of last season?

Seeing that tweet pop up on my phone confirming that we were champions. I didn't make it to Merthyr and was playing with my son in my back garden when the confirmation came. The sense of relief and happiness was overwhelming, I was so glad we didn't have to rely on the play-offs.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Probably an unlikely pick, but I'd go with Jack Evans at Harrogate. We need a couple of left backs this summer and Jack actually spent a short time on loan with us back in 2022.

From what I've seen he has mainly played in midfield for Harrogate but I'd have him on the left hand side of our back four. He brings a really good work ethic, solid in the fundamentals for a full back and isn't afraid to get forward either. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

I'm sure Craig doesn't need my advice after the success of last season, but after seeing us promoted into the National League twice before I'd just say have absolutely no fear at all. We've earned our place in this league on merit and more than deserve to be here. We have real quality in the players we kept on from last season and they're more than capable of having us right up there again come May next year.

Show the rest of the league what we can do and that we've learned from the past mistakes. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? I love Mill Farm, it's a superb venue for Non-league football, but if I had one criticism though it would be the roof on the main stand.

I know it's due to the hotel and corporate facilities being on the first floor but during the winter and when it's raining there is absolutely no protection at all. A lower roof also helps add to the atmosphere especially in big games. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

The Coasters of course! If I was pushed for a non-biased answer though I think you have to look at Carlisle United now that York and Rochdale are gone, and with some changes coming at Southend. I actually think the league is a bit weaker overall than last year with the two outstanding sides gone, but I can't see any other side that has as big an argument to be champions as Carlisle.

Who’ll be the surprise package? Taking bias out of it again, I genuinely think it could be us. Everyone (quite lazily) expects us to be right in and around the bottom four next season but if they looked at our season in a bit more detail I don't think they would - 100 points, a record breaking 112 goals scored, records for both home and away consecutive victories and some fantastic young talents both upfront and at the back.

We've kept everyone we wanted to this summer and with those yet to sign our squad will be stronger come August. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We're the only team to have won both the FA Vase and FA Trophy, in 2008 and 2019 respectively.

PHOTOS BY AIDAN WILSON

article.title: The Fans' View: 'There's rarely a dull moment at Aldershot Town!'
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
It's not often that there's not something going on at Aldershot Town, and the last 12 months or so is certainly proof of that. New ownership amid a topsy turvy campaign which started with high hopes under Tommy Widdrington after Wembley FA Trophy glory. He had quit by October, and before the end of the season John Coleman had gone too - little over a week after owner Deane Wood said that he would "definitely" be at the club next season.

What will the next campaign under former Slough Town manager and ex-Shots midfielder Scott Davies hold? Fresh from his 60th birthday celebrations, BBC Surrey’s knowledgeable Rob Worrall talks us through it. Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season?

Crazy Lows & Highs! What ground did you love visiting the most Truro City Stadium. Firstly, it was the only new ground I commentated from for BBC Surrey this season.

Great atmosphere and vibe on the night. High drama too, with the unfortunate sending off of Marcus Dewhurst (later rescinded), and late penalty drama as nine man Shots - Will Nightingale had to hobble off after all subs had been used - grabbed a late leveller thanks to James Henry’s penalty! Who was your club’s Player of the Season?

Whilst Ryan Hill and Will Nightingale scooped up the club awards between them (deservedly so), my personal favourite was Olly Scott. He excelled once back from a shoulder injury at left-back and immediately hitting the required levels, Olly showed incredible determination & bravery in the tackle, twice playing on with his head bandaged and also weighing in with a composed cracker of a finish in Aldershot’s commanding away display at Yeovil. Whoever signs him will have added a wonderful player and human being into their ranks.

What was the single best moment of last season? The crazy five minutes in which Shots came from 2-0 down at home to FC Halifax Town to score three goals and turn the game on its head! Two-goal Charlie Warren and Will Nightingale scored.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? It would have been Jack Nolan, who has now signed for Hartlepool United. A class act and a cut above most of the rest in the division!

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? You’re building a Shots team that will play the way in which you believe we can be successful. Young, hungry, pacy and powerful.

The Red & Blue Army will get behind you from the off. During any hard times, stick to your beliefs, ensure the players leave it all out there each week and let’s get the EBB rocking! What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

Nothing - it’s a proper old school football stadium, with a terrific atmosphere, particularly in the Eastbank. I’d love another 1,000 people in there supporting us though! It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

It feels much tougher to predict than last season, but Carlisle United have made a shrewd appointment in Rob Elliott, who knows the league and what’s required so so well now. With a huge fan base too, a sizeable high quality squad and the financial clout to strengthen as required in the second half of the season, they will probably start as favourites for me. However, very few playing squads are complete just yet, so let’s see how they are all looking come August 9.

Who’ll be the surprise package? Hartlepool and Sutton have both signed well to date, so perhaps one of them - or Woking, for whom Jermain Defoe’s tenure began well and they’ve added some quality over the summer too. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

That this season Aldershot Town will be marking a century of football at ‘The Rec’ with a special Centenary shirt, khaki coloured to emphasise the clubs strong military connections. PHOTOS: IAN MORSMAN

article.title: The Fans' View: Alty have a glittering history, and a fantastic future
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
There was much sadness registered when Altrincham decided Phil Parkinson’s time was up back in late October. After more than eight years, an era came to a close. The division’s longest serving manager was no more with the club far too close to the drop zone for comfort.

A campaign predicted to be full of excitement didn’t go to plan, but under Neil Gibson they finished with a flourish and managed to secure a heartening top half finish. We’re asking the fans of every team the same ten questions as we find out a little more about the past ten months, and what makes their club so special. There are few supporters with more knowledge of their club than Phil James.

The end of the season maybe came too soon for fast-improving Altrincham and here’s what the patron and Moss Lane regular made of it all. Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? Things gradually improved!

What ground did you love visiting the most I always enjoy trips to Wealdstone who, along with Alty, were one of the founder members of the first National League (Alliance Premier League) back in 1979. Both sets of fans share a friendly camaraderie and respect for each other with most of our games unsegregated so fans can enjoy 'old school' non-league etiquette of changing ends at half time if they wish. Who was your club’s Player of the Season?

Alty officially had three 'Players of the Season' at their Awards night - Matty Kosylo (Manager's choice), Luke Hutchinson (Players' choice), and Tylor Golden (Fans' choice) My own vote went to goalkeeper Luke Hutchinson, who was on a season long loan from Bolton, and was 22 years old when he came... In the absence of experienced keeper Ethan Ross (out all season with an ACL injury) his performances gradually improved throughout his loan and he was outstanding during the second half of the season - Luke did win our 'Young Player of the Year' award. What was the single best moment of last season?

For many fans it will be the end to the Alty home game against Scunthorpe with the latter stages played in heavy rain and sleet. Alty were 1-2 down going into the last minute of normal time but found the fight necessary to win 4-2 (scoring on 89, 90+1, 90+5 mins) - brilliant! If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Alty need one or two forwards (as Jimmy Knowles and Olly Crankshaw mainly play off the wing) I would like to bring Scunthorpe striker Declan Howe back to Altrincham. He played eight games on loan for Alty last season scoring four goals and would be a perfect fit. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

Firstly, i'd like to thank Neil Gibson for saving Alty from potential relegation after stepping in after long serving Phil Parkinson departed. I would then ask that he endeavours to address our issue of conceding so many late goals resulting in dropped points. We seem to make too many late substitutions (assume with the intention of bringing fresh legs on to protect points) but this often backfired last season as the team then went too defensive, inviting pressure, which quite often led to the opposition scoring.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? The away end needs a roof as it is the only area of the stadium without one. A roof has been mooted a few times going back to 1967 but to date this has still not become reality.

This means that away fans standing on the large open terrace get soaked if it rains! It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Most seem to think it will be between Carlisle United, Southend and Forest Green Rovers.

If I had to choose, I'd go with Carlisle who were third last season and now have Rob Elliot who performed the 'great escape' with Gateshead last season. Who’ll be the surprise package? Gateshead.

They had a brilliant run towards the end of last season winning nine and drawing four of their last 17 games to stay up. Despite losing manager Rob Elliot to Carlisle they could build on last season and make the playoffs. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

Altrincham FC are one of only four Non-League teams in the history of the FA Cup to win away at top division opposition since the present FA Cup format was introduced over 100 years ago in 1925. Alty beat then top division Birmingham City 2-1 at St.Andrew's in the FA Cup 3rd Round in 1986.

article.title: Welcome to the Enterprise National League: Barrow
article.author: Tom Scott
article.html:
Here is the lowdown on Enterprise National League Barrow ahead of the new season. Factfile Last Season: 24th - League Two Top Scorer: Josh Gordon (9) Manager: Adam Murray Ground: Holker Street Best National League Performance: Champions* How they got here... Barrow had been EFL mainstays for half a century – until suffering relegation to the Northern Premier League in 1972.

They would become founder members of the Alliance Premier League in 1979, and yo-yoed between the top two tiers of non-league football for four decades, winning the FA Trophy in 1990 and again in 2010. They were Conference North champions in 2014-15 and spent five seasons in the National League before the 2019-20 season was suspended by Covid-19, with Barrow four points clear at the top. When the season was eventually declared curtailed, they were crowned champions via points-per-game, returning to the Football League after 48 years.

Six seasons in League Two followed, with the club establishing itself as a stable if presence in the division's lower reaches. But the 2025-26 campaign unravelled badly, and none of the five managers that took charge across the campaign could arrest the slide. Despite playing catch-up for most of the season, it took until the final day until they were mathematically confirmed as exiting the EFL after a six-year spell.

Keep an eye out for... Prolific frontman Alex Reid was the first man through the door after new boss Adam Murray joined the Bluebirds. A proven goalscorer in the National League, he averaged almost a goal every three games last season for Hartlepool United.

*Final league positions determined on PPG due to Coronavirus pandemic Main Image – Barrow AFC

article.title: The Fans View: Boreham Wood taking first step on road to redemption
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
How do you go about recovering after being seconds from winning a place in the EFL for the very first time? No amount of holidays, family time or soul searching this summer would wipe out Mani Dieseruvwe‘s thunderous header with time nearly up. Boreham Wood have picked themselves up from the Wembley canvas before of course, and Luke Garrard has to summon the strength to do it again.

It still stings, but as they say: there’s always next season. We put the questions to Phillip Thomas , who hopes the club’s Promotion Final heartache can act as a spur one football resumes. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Not.

Looking. Back. Fixture release day is on Friday July 10 - who’s your ideal first day opponent?

An August return to Carlisle United I think. They will be the main contenders you we’ll take them while they are trying to find their feet. What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season?

Wembley again! In all seriousness I want to do more away matches next season and there’s a lot of northern teams replacing those who went up but I am looking forward to Worthing, a new ground for me and most National League fans next season. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in You know who I am going to say but I’m not sure we could resist a club record bid!

Abdul Abdulmalik. He is going far. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

Just keep doing what you are doing. The pride you have in this club will never be felt by any other Wood manager. I would just say what you suffered at Wembley x two will be worth it when the moment comes.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? The stadium is fantastic and there’s plans in place to do even more. Let’s try an encourage locals even more by offering more ticket specials and even a pay what you want game.

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? You can’t look much further than Carlisle United but I might be wrong. But I get the feeling Dale Vince and Forest Green Rovers just can’t repeat last year.

They’ll know they have to challenge. Who’ll be the surprise package? The pressure will be off Southend United with a number of key departures and Kieron Dyer will get time to transition and the lack of pressure could work in their favour.

Also AFC Fylde could but this year’s Scunthorpe United and Boreham Wood - going up and hitting the play-offs. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? How many people you ask will answer Abdul Abdulmalik I wonder!

I’ll do for Regan Linney. He would be excellent with Matt Rush in our attack. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

Luke Garrard first walked into the club over 20 years ago as a player. Ten years later he became our manager and ten years after that nearly took us to the EFL.

article.title: The Fans' View: The Pilgrims' choice is for more Boston excitement!
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
You’d have thought you would have to go some for Boston United fans to enjoy this summer quite as much as they did the last one. Fuelled by their incredible escape - a total transformation spearheaded by manager Graham Coughlin - surely the sense of excitement and pride couldn’t be matched, what with the famous second season syndrome and all that? Well, after the Pilgrims’ top half finish and fine late season form with Paul Hurst back calling the shots, you’d argue than there’s even more anticipation for the big kick off.

Hurst of course returned in January after a near-15 year absence. Some of the club’s faithful weren’t impressed at first - he left in 2011 under a bit of a cloud. It’ll be hard to find a supporter not happy now!

The Boston United Fan Page are certainly on board and they look forward with a bit of looking back as the club look for a fourth campaign to really remember in a row. Sum up your club's summer so far in three words Patient. Methodical.

Promising. Fixture release day is on Friday July 10 - who's your ideal first day opponent? Harrogate or Barrow.

They're the two sides coming down from League Two and it would be a great early benchmark for where we're at. Why not get straight into a big test on day one? What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season?

Scunthorpe United. It's one of the shorter trips for us and recent visits have always been enjoyable. A good away day and usually a decent atmosphere too.

What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in? Tom Cursons. We've already seen a couple of key players move on this summer, so keeping hold of Cursons would be huge.

He's someone you can build a team around. You've got two minutes alone with your club's manager - what advice would you give him? Honestly, none.

Paul Hurst knows far more about football than I ever will. The only thing I'd say is if another club comes calling, make sure you have a chat with David Newton first! What's the one thing you would change about your team's stadium?

The height of the terracing. I'd love to see the three terrace stands elevated a bit more. The views behind the goals can be tricky at times and a few extra rows would make a massive difference.

I'll stop there before I start sounding like a certain Pilgrims fan! It's early days but who's winning the league in 2026/27? Scunthorpe.

It pains me to say it, but they're recruiting really well. They were already one of the strongest sides around and look like they've improved again. They'll take some stopping.

Who'll be the surprise package? Kidderminster Harriers. A lot depends on their recruitment, but promoted teams can often carry momentum into the new season and I wouldn't be shocked to see them exceed expectations.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Abdul Abdulmalik. He was one of the standout players in the league last season.

Direct, exciting and capable of producing moments of quality, exactly the sort of player supporters love watching. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? A lot of opposition fans don't realise just how much Boston United has achieved off the pitch in recent years.

The club led the development of the Jakemans Community Stadium, secured the funding to make it happen and has now completed all four stands (nearly). Even more impressively, the club is now pretty much debt-free, something that's increasingly rare in modern football. PHOTOS: TIM HOFF

article.title: The Fans' View: Carlisle hope it is sweeter second time around
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
It was meant to be written in the stars for Carlisle United when they arrived last summer. It was 20 years from their last fleeting visit, when they became one of the select few clubs to secure an immediate return. Things don’t always work out how you plan, but they do say the longer it takes to get back up to the EFL, the harder it becomes.

They’re going to try again under a new manager as Rob Elliot replacing Mark Hughes. He knows he needs to hit the ground running. In our latest fan preview, Cumbrians supporter Tom Walton talks high expectations and what needs to be done before the season kicks off.

Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Decent summer window. We have strengthened in the areas we needed to, apart from in the goalkeeping department. Hopefully we can get a couple more in before the start of the season.

What are your exceptions for next season? The aim has to be promotion, it wont be easy as there are a few good sides that we'll have to be wary of. Given that we haven't really lost any of our best players and with our fantastic support I think it’s a realistic aim.

We need to get our club and supporters back in the EFL as soon as possible. What ground are you looking forward to visiting? I’m looking forward to visiting a few grounds I’ve not done before this season - AFC Fylde and Tamworth in particular.

What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in Morgan Feeney. He is our captain and an absolute warrior at the back. We look so much more solid when he is in the team.

He’s a must-keep in my opinion. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? To have our team play progressive football with no fear.

Last year we were too negative in certain games which ultimately meant we came up slightly short in the play-offs. We shouldn't be fearing any team in this division. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

We need to invest in the Warwick Road End and Paddock in the same way we did with the East Stand last year. Our atmosphere is normally brilliant, but these investments would help the noise levels even more. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

Carlisle of course! We have to deal with the pressure of being title favourites though, and we don’t like doing things the easy way. The biggest challengers I think will be Hartlepool or Southend, both clubs have recruited very well so far this summer.

Who’ll be the surprise package? AFC Fylde. They had a very strong campaign in the National League North last year and play some very good football.

I can see them surprising a few this season and challenging the top half. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Abdul Abdulmalik.

He tore us apart in the play-offs last season with his pace and technical ability. One of the best in this division, and I can see EFL teams showing interest in him. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

We have reached the final of the EFL trophy more then any other club, winning it twice in 1997 and 2011.

article.title: The Fans' View: Are Eastleigh edgy or does pre-season count for little?
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
They say pre-season results count for nothing, and Eastleigh certainly hope that rings true. Six games, six defeats. A problem, or simply keeping their powder dry?

Matt Gray has a point to prove after his time at Eastbourne Borough was cut short after just three months - but a manager with National League title winning experience knows how to motivate. He sees no reason why the Spitfires can’t soar once the real stuff gets going. We asked fan Luke James for his thoughts ahead of the big kick-off on Saturday.

Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words. Quiet, uncertain, uncomfortable. What are your expectations for next season - and are they achievable?

This season, I think survival has to be the main aim. If we can stay up comfortably, avoid a relegation battle, and continue improving as a team then I would see that as a successful campaign. What ground are you looking forward to visiting?

Aldershot, because of the fierce rivalry and the atmosphere those games always bring. There’s always a bit extra on the line, which makes it one of the best away days of the season. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in Aaron Blair, 100 per cent.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Trust the squad you’ve built, and don’t be afraid to give young players like Connor Underhill opportunities. Keep us playing on the front foot, fans appreciate positive football.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Improving the East Stand and making it more like the South Stand. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

I’m backing Carlisle United. Big club, strong squad and they’ll be desperate to get back into the Football League. Who’ll be the surprise package?

I feel like Worthing will do better than expected. They have done some great business this summer in my opinion. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Regan Linney, Carlisle United’s striker. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? They probably wouldn’t know how much the club has grown and how much potential there is here.

article.title: The Fans' View: FC Halifax will have to prove tipsers wrong again
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
It seems that more summers than not FC Halifax Town go into a new campaign having a point to prove to everyone. Whether it’s the loss of some key players, ground issues or a manager saying goodbye, close seasons rarely run smoothly at the Shay. This time they have had to contend with all three but in John McGrath they have appointed a manager who is determined to steady the ship.

They also have a habit of casting aside the negatives and surprising people - and they’ll need to this time as well. Shaymen superfan Steven Ledgard previews 2026/27 as we put him on the spot with 18 days to go until we kick off. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Disappointing, poor, concerning What are your expectations for next season - and can they be achieved?

With us losing Turner, Cooke, Harris and Smith on the pitch and Lakeland off of it I think ultimately the long term goal of EFL football isn't realistic this season. I’m hoping we manage to get mid-table for 26/27 and can keep new manager John McGrath to then push on in 27/28. What ground are you looking forward to visiting?

I’ve got a few new grounds that I'm excited for, Worthing in particular will be what I'm most looking forward to, hopefully be a good day out on the south coast as it'll be a new ground for me and the longer away days with my mates are always good. But then Harrogate on Boxing Day will be another great one because it's another new ground for me and we'll likely take 600 fans, or so and it'll hopefully be a good atmosphere. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in If I had to pick just one it would be Cody Johnson.

He was one of our best players last season and with the two players better than him last year in Jay Turner-Cooke and Will Harris both leaving, keeping the next best player is definitely a priority. A lot of the squad were good last season, and it'd be a shame to lose any of them. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

Don't listen to the fans too much, some of our supporter base are very reactionary and harsh. Success will always take time with a budget like ours and some fans at the club expect top seven every season with wins every week, so sometimes it's important to drown them out. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

Hard to pick just one, there's a lot that could be improved with the stadium. I think I'd go for finally getting a proper scoreboard installed and to bring us slightly into the 21st century! Either that or get card machines on the turnstile finally and make it easier for more fans to come through the gates.

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Carlisle United are my favourites right now. Arguably the biggest club in the league - either them or southend take that prize - and they have what I feel is the most complete squad.

A lot of teams have added some real quality though and will be up there. Southend, Hartlepool and Boreham Wood will all give Carlisle a run for their money but I do feel the Cumbrians have the best squad overall and the support to get them over the line. Who’ll be the surprise package?

Yeovil Town. They have already made some very decent additions like Spasov from Southend and while I don't think they will win the play-offs or push for the title, I can see them surprising people and finishing in the top seven. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Regan Linney from Carlisle. Pretty self explanatory since he's one of the best forwards in the league and with Harris leaving for Hartlepool I haven't been too impressed with the replacements we've signed so far. Linney is a proven goalscorer that could play striker or cover out wide.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? In 1980 we managed to beat Manchester City in the FA Cup, arguably the club’s best ever result (if we consider the old liquidated AFC Halifax and the Phoenix FC Halifax as the same club)

article.title: The Fans' View: Why it could be a case of quality over quantity at Forest Green
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Manager Robbie Savage says Forest Green Rovers’ summer recruitment is just about done. By this point last year, it had barely even started. Some 17 players have already departed the New Lawn, with six coming in.

Savage has heard all the jokes about the relentless wave of new additions during his first year at the club, and this time it appears to be a case of quality over quantity. So no new signing every week, perhaps! Fans hope the less-is-more approach pays off after the club fell short of expectation last time around.

This close season we are asking a fan from every club to preview the new campaign and Rovers regular Michael Dwaine answers our burning questions with four weeks to go. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Much less hectic. What are your expectations for next season - and can they be achieved?

I can’t remember the last time the answer to this wasn’t promotion. It’s not worked out for a while but that must be the aim after a poor year last year. What ground are you looking forward to visiting?

Worthing. I missed the FA Cup game last season and it will be great to spent the day there on the coast in the August sunshine [...you watch it rain and we lose 3-0] What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in It was Tom Knowles but that’s out the window.

Kyle McAllister is really important to what we do and how the team performs. He was linked away in January but thankfully he stayed. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

If you would have asked me the question in May it would have been easy - sort the squad out early and stop the relentless signings. Robbie probably didn’t need telling and there appears to be a plan in place. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

I would like our fans to be able to swap ends at half-time. It would really boost the atmosphere. I’m not sure how that would work with the away fans positioned where they are.

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Boreham Wood. It’s a rogue shout but they have kept their squad together and will think it’s time one of the smaller clubs won the league again.

If they do keep Abdul Abdulmalik they have easily the best player in the league. It’s open this year. Who’ll be the surprise package?

Tamworth have had some investment by the looks of it. Nobody likes playing there, especially us! If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

We don’t like signing new players! Abdulmalik obviously, but Matt Rush from Boreham Wood would also fit in brilliantly. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

Our players are not forced to be vegan, despite what most away fans think! They can eat meat, but just not when they are at the club as it’s 100 per cent plant based.

article.title: The Fans' View: Gateshead in need of another summer re-set
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
It’s another summer re-set for Gateshead, but if ever a club was well-versed on a rebuild, it’s them. For the second time, manager Rob Elliot has left the International Stadium after his team’s achievements were noticed elsewhere. Few things are ever sure for Heed fans, but one thing is next season - their side will not lack bite.

Tough-tackling former Middlesbrough and Sunderland midfielder Lee Cattermole has been named as the new head coach and with many of the squad who pulled off a brilliant escape last season also off, he can make it his own. Gateshead fan Jay Fitzgerald answers some key questions after another challenging close season. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words An underwhelming start.

Fixture release day is on Friday July 10 - who’s your ideal first day opponent? An early test against Hartlepool United. A stern start against local opposition for a new manager trying to find his feet.

Also I quite like beating Hartlepool! What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season? I’m looking forward to visiting Harrogate, a new ground for myself with a welcome couple of new northern additions to the league.

What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in It has to be Adam Desbois, a safe pair of hands and will play in the EFL someday. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Take each game as it comes, stick with playing out from the back and keeping the club’s identity.

This will make it easier to keep the fans on side. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Not really sure where to start with this one.

We could do with putting more club signage around the stadium and making it feel more like home. We need to get more locals in to support the team It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Hate to state the obvious but I can’t see past Carlisle, naming Rob Elliot as the manager with a huge budget and good squad will make it hard for any other team to compete.

Who’ll be the surprise package? I fancy Woking to really surprise the big boys. Ended the season very well and with a few decent additions could be a strong outfit.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Regan Linney would be a massive signing for anyone in the division, he’s a proven goalscorer for the level and a goalscorer will win you league titles so it’d go with him. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

That the Heed are massive!!!

article.title: The Fans' View: Landon's American dream has Hartlepool believing again
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
For the first time in a long time, Hartlepool United fans are wishing the summer away. That’s because for the best part of five years, the close season has been a good distraction. Quite often, football wasn’t an escape for fans from their worries.

But that all changed last season. New owner, the American Landon Smith, completed his takeover and said he wanted to "have fun". He’s not the only one.

Pools fan Jack Gardner is counting down the days to kick-off and hasn’t been excited for quite some time. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Outstanding and Impressive What are your expectations for next season - and are they realistic? Expectations for this next season are definitely to be comfortably in a play-off position and to get promoted back to the EFL.

I think these are very realistic with the signings we have made! What ground are you looking forward to visiting? I’m looking forward to going to Hornchurch’s ground next season, it’s a new one to tick off and reminds me of a proper Non-League heritage ground.

What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in One player I would not want to lose this summer would be Jamie Miley. He is a really good playmaker and can have a big impact on the game. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

The advice I would give to Lee Clark is to be honest to us fans and grow that relationship and play some attractive attacking football to get people off their seats. We want him to enjoy his time here and we are all hoping for the same outcome. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

That would have to be an update to our scoreboard. It has seen better days. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

I’ll have to say my team Hartlepool United, but if i was being non biased I would have to say Carlisle or Southend. Who’ll be the surprise package? Yeovil will be the team to spring a few surprises, they’ve made some very good signings so far.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? If I could sign one player from any team in the division - it would be tough to course one - but I’d probably go with Abdul Abdulmalik from Boreham Wood. The man is a menace.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? One thing that opposition fans may not know about our club is that we were once nearly bought by Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney before they decided to buy Wrexham instead.

article.title: The Fans' View:  'Hornchurch won't sit around and let people writing our club off stop us'
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Hornchurch seem determined to do things their way this season - and don’t seem to care what anyone else thinks. While manager Daryl McMahon is looking to weaponise their modest Bridge Avenue home, supporters know that while their team may not be trendy, they’re going to try very hard for the shirt. The Essex club are up into the National League and they seem happy to let others do the talking.

It’s back to business next weekend, and the Urchins start against Kidderminster Harriers in a battle of the Promotion Final winning sides. Peter Hay thinks people are already underestimating Hornchurch - and that could be a costly mistake! Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Busy, Exciting, Optimistic.

What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season? Hard to pick out as almost all the grounds are new to Hornchurch, but possibly The Shay at FC Halifax Town as it looks interesting and some of the fans have already been in touch about sharing a few beers there, so it's nice to feel welcome to a new league so quickly. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in There are a few I could name, as we have a squad of players who work hard for each other.

Angelo Balanta was player of the season - club and supporters. So I will say him as he has been outstanding at the club with all of the players, staff and fans; we would all miss him. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

I don't think I could give the gaffer any advice as he knows what he is doing already and has the backing of the club. I think all I would say is keep being yourself and keep doing what you have already done for the club, no matter how tough the season gets, and thanks for choosing to manage our team; it has been an amazing two-and-a-half seasons, and I hope he can keep writing more success into the club's history. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

Can I get away with two? Have the Council allow the club to own and redevelop the stadium to make better grounds and facility. The second is to have the rules on drinking in sight of the pitch got rid of, as our bar terrace overlooking the pitch was a great place to watch a game without rushing to finish your beer.

We will lose that this season, which on our best days added a bit of a different atmosphere which will be missed. Who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Not sure, but possibly one from Carlisle United, Scunthorpe, Southend or Boreham Wood who are all busy rebuilding and I am sure they are all going to aim for the title this season.

Who’ll be the surprise package? Hornchurch. Nobody has given the team a chance in their predictions so far to even stay up.

All I will say to that is that the team we have and the players brought in this summer is a team that is not going to sit around and let people writing us off stop them. They will play football their way and won't be dictated to and the players that have come in so far will all bring their experience to a young squad and will use the fact we have been written off to motivate themselves. I would not be surprised to see us finish midtable or better, and I believe that we will stay up as this club grows bigger and bigger with its new investors, sponsors and more fans coming along season by season.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? I don't really know many players at this league level but I would say that having added some new defenders to build from the back line has been key to our close season so signing Joe Kizzi, Frankie Moralee, Jack Baldwin and Ryan Inniss all of which have been at this level and higher may well prove to be the solid back line we need to have a solid season. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

Most fans will probably be unaware that we won the FA Trophy in 2020/2021 and went to Wembley just as Covid rules were lifted. That was an incredible achievement back then and cemented in place the ambition of the chairman to not just own a club but build the club up. That, for me, was the big milestone that showed we could compete at this level.

article.title: The Fans' View: Harriers hope to stick around a little long this time!
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
There’s a running joke within the Kidderminster Harriers fan base that they are the epitome of a club that can never resist doing things the hard way. Many were nodding along with them when promotion winning manager Adam Murray left to join Barrow days after their greatest moment in years. Kiddy are about to return to the National League following a two year absence - and they need to make a better fist of it that they didn’t the last time.

It was a fleeting visit in 2023/24 and Paul Wotton won’t sit back and allow a repeat performance. We asked Jackie Oldham to set the scene with the new campaign only days away. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Departures, rebuilding, hope What are your expectations for next season - and are they realistic?

I am always fairly positive about Harriers (to the annoyance of some), but if we aim for midtable, if it goes a bit wobbly at least we have breathing space. 18th would be fine. What ground are you looking forward to visiting?

It was going up be Harrogate, but that's a Tuesday night so I can't get to that. I have Forest Green on my radar, mainly due to their veggie food - can be hard to come by in many grounds. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in A lot of ours have gone (Obi, Foulkes et al).

If I was to pick one from the remaining ones I'd say David Digga Davis. Leads by example, runs the the midfield like the true professional he is. Scored some vital goals last season too.

He is becoming a club legend. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Keep the fans on your side, as on our day we are your 12th man.

Be honest, especially when things aren't going well. Harriers fans are always happier when they are informed. Paul Wotton is already ticking these boxes for me.

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? I am going with Scunthorpe United - they were pretty good last season, now they should go for it. Who’ll be the surprise package?

I'm hoping us, as we have been written off by many. If not us, Boston United, They have made some smart signings. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Kieran Donnelly from Tamworth, obviously! What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We played the first FA Cup game under floodlights in 1955, v Brierley Hill Alliance.

article.title: The Fans' View: Not any old Iron! Scunthorpe looking up again
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
After a few years of strife and disconnect, Scunthorpe United fans are smiling again. Following promotion in 2024/25, they went hunting another last season and a talented and committed bunch of players nearly delivered against the odds. Our close season mega mission of speaking to a supporter of every club to get their views on last season, next season and everything in between is ramping up.

We’re asking each of the fans the same ten questions as we find out a little more about the past ten months, and what makes their club so special. Barra, the host of the Iron Hour podcast , has kindly filled us in on everything going on at the Attis Arena. Here’s what he has to say after another season to remember at Scunthorpe United.

Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? Huge over achievement. What ground did you love visiting the most York City's LNER Community Stadium was a huge standout for me!

To beat the eventful champions on a Tuesday night in a localish game was very, very special. The fans that night were unbelievable and there is something about football under the lights that does it for me and it was arguably our best performance of the season too. Who was your club’s Player of the Season?

Uncontroversially, I will say Callum Roberts. His 27 goal involvements were the difference between a bang average season and one which exceeded all expectations. His ability to take a man on at will and either cut inside to get that shot away or to take the ball the byline and put the ball into the danger area is simply exceptional.

His move to the EFL is fully deserved and there won't be a single Iron fan who begrudges the move up. What was the single best moment of last season? Having already mentioned York, I will say the scenes at full time after we beat Southend in the play-off Eliminator.

The owners of the club were visibly moved, seeing one of them in tears on the pitch celebrating with the players reminded us all of just how far this club has come in recent years. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? With Zain Westbrooke leaving and Oli Ewing having not yet committed to us, I would love to see us bring Cody Johnson in from Halifax.

He is tenacious, vocal and his ability to dictate the pace of the game has impressed me every time I have seen him play. There will be some more glamorous and obvious players but in my opinion those ratty midfielders take you to a different level. With age on his side, I could see him playing in a decent EFL side one day.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Great question! I'm not sure he would be advised to listen to an emotional fan like me as he seems to have things well under control.

I would take the opportunity to thank him, he has taken us from National League North and made us legitimate prospects for an EFL return. Keep doing what you're doing and I respect the attention deflection at times, it takes the heat off the players. Club legend!

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Another great question! I would extend the Iron Bar, this would mean the queueing time would be cut and we could make better use of the room during the World Cup and other major football games.

All any fans wants is a pint and a few goals! It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Carlisle look to have a very decent chance this season, a huge club with a huge fanbase.

They have shuffled the deck with the departure of Mark Hughes so they look to be taking it seriously once again. Who’ll be the surprise package? My dark horses to challenge them would be Yeovil, I could see them building a squad to challenge for the play-offs as a minimum.

If they can attract a few more players, they could make Huish Park a fortress. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Three ex-Scunthorpe players have gone on to captain England.....

That's Kevin Keegan, Ray Clemence and......Ian Botham. That one always comes up in a pub quiz and catches non Iron fans out!

article.title: The Fans' View: How a big early call sparked Solihull's season
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
In a season like no other for managerial movement, Solihull Moors fans are happy that their owners bit the bullet. Chris Millington replaced Matt Taylor, who was fired just a few weeks into last campaign with the team sitting bottom. The new man had a big impact and quickly steered the club clear of problems.

The Moors are used to life near the top and losing play-off finalists in two of the past four seasons, they are now plotting another push. Callum Moseley, a football writer on the National League Lowdown , has followed the club’s fortunes and saw a big improvement. We put to him some key questions about his club and asked what he would say to manager Millington if he ever wanted some advice!

Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? Progress. Mixed.

Frustration. What ground did you love visiting the most? For me, I’m a sucker for a proper Non-League ground, and for that reason it has to be Tamworth.

Food vans, terraces, the traditional Non-League feel and the fact it’s local meaning Solihull always take a good amount there. Who was your club’s Player of the Season? I could go boring and go with the deserving name which would be Alex Whitmore, but I’ll go different and say Darius Lipsiuc.

Sent off just six minutes into his debut, but went on to hit double figures for goal contributions and end as one of the first names on the team sheet, quite remarkable really. What was the single best moment of last season? Whilst the two games against Carlisle were very good, I think there’s only one answer you can give here and that’s the 7-1 victory against Tamworth on Boxing Day.

A Joe Sbarra hat-trick always makes a good day even better, first time we’d scored seven in a league game for a considerable amount of time and topped off what had been a brilliant run of results at the time. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? I’d love to say someone like Abdul Abdulmalik but I don’t think that’s entirely realistic sadly, so instead I’ll go with his team-mate Lewis Richardson.

He’s a versatile forward that can operate as a striker or right winger, an area in which Solihull desperately need to strengthen this summer. We need an individual who’s good on the ball, scores goals, creates chances and can take a game by the scruff of its neck and deliver results. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

Great question - to answer it simply it would be more of the same please. There has been a noticeable improvement in quality since his arrival, and had it not been for a mid-season hiatus in terms of our winless run, we’d have pushed for the play-offs. My message would be to ensure that the spine of the side is as strong as it can be, then focus on the wider options after.

On a personal note, I’d also ask him to start Oscar Rutherford - a player the fans adore but hasn’t necessarily had a look in under Chris Millington so far. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Think if I’m honest here, it would have to be the ‘temporary’ feel that runs down one side of the stadium.

I’m aware of course that building a new stand would require significant investment which would only likely arise with a promotion to the EFL, but I feel that the temporary seating makes the stadium feel less like a home if I’m honest. It’s early days, but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? I’d anticipate that most people will probably say Carlisle here, but for me if they can retain their key players I think Boreham Wood have a great shot.

They have the best manager in the division in my opinion, countless talented players and all of which are tied down to contracts that would require fees to get out of. They score plenty of goals, defend really well as a unit and of course have Luke Garrard, they’ll be strong contenders next season. Who’ll be the surprise package?

I said this on Twitter already, but I’m really tempted to say Yeovil Town. They have an ambitious young manager who’s driven to succeed, a lot of their key assets are also under contract, which can be built around over the summer - not to mention their recruitment in large quantities has been very successful in recent months. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

Many people know that Solihull Moors is one of the youngest full-time side in English football, but most don’t actually know why the merger happened. In early 2005, an unfortunate arson attack at Moor Green’s stadium caused the main stand and clubhouse to go up in flames, forcing them to relocate to Solihull Borough. However, the gate receipts were severely impacted and both teams struggled financially - thus agreeing to join together to form the club we know today as Solihull Moors.

article.title: The Fans' View: Memories to cherish, but Southend sail into a bright new era
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
It’s all change at Southend United this summer as the club put distance between themselves and their recent past. Gone is Kevin Maher, a legend at the club whose time ended in fitting fashion with their Wembley FA Trophy triumph. Gone too are a number of the players who stepped up in challenging times, like free-scoring wing-back Gus Scott-Morriss and goalkeeper Collin Andeng Ndi.

Kieron Dyer has been entrusted to usher in a new era at Roots Hall, and impressive recruitment points at a possible challenge for promotion. The supporters are strapped in and ready for another shot reclaiming their EFL place and we put the important questions to long-term fan Sarah Prendergast. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words.

A fresh start. Fixture release day is on Friday July 10 - who’s your ideal first day opponent? I would have said Truro City if they were still here as I’m in Cornwall on the opening weekend.

I can probably make it to Yeovil Town so that would be ideal please! What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season? Yeovil on August 8!

Failing that Hornchurch if I can get a ticket. We all heard a lot about Bridge Avenue especially on social meadia after they won promotion. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in?

Well we have lost three of the players I didn’t want lose so I’m going to keep quiet and hope nobody else leaves! You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Just live and breathe Southend United like the fans do.

In all honestly Keiron Dyer wouldn’t have been top of many fans’ lists but sometimes a person without the connection is the right answer. It’s an open division this year and so far his signings are really impressive. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

There is so much to love about Roots Hall but also so much that needs to be done. Being able to use the internet on your phone in 2026 is a great place to start I would say. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

A lot of people are saying Carlisle United but I don’t think they’re stronger than last season. I have a little feeling Forest Green might be big contenders and Hartlepool are another club going for it. If we start well who knows.

Who’ll be the surprise package? Yeovil Town could do well. I've said them a lot so far.

A lot of changes but Joe Gubbins turning down a new contract from us goes to show they’re expecting a promotion challenge. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Abdul Abdulmalik from Boreham Wood is the obvious answer but I would love to see Zak Brunt at Southend.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? The legend that is Bobby Moore managed the club from 1984-1986. Unlike us, boardroom battles saw tenure come to an end.

article.title: The Fans' View: Does Sutton's signing fast-start mean they're a surprise package?
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Sutton United’s hopes of flying under the radar next season could already be over after some shrewd early summer business. Charlie Carter, Temi Babalola, Manny Osadebe, Jordan Moore-Taylor and Will Nightingale’s arrival have already seen the club thrust into more than one ‘surprise package’ conversation. Mike Dowling from the The Sutton Podcast couldn’t resist the temptation, and has selected his club to raise some eyebrows next term.

He’s been telling us all about last season, a campaign to forget at Gander Green Lane, and the next one which is already looking promising as Chris Agutter gets his feet under the table. In our latest Fan View, Mike explains that low expectations may not be a bad thing and why a Messi moment will be hard to better once football finally resumes. Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season?

Must. Do. Better.

What ground did you love visiting the most I don’t really do many away games so it’s a bit of a cheat to say Wealdstone.. because it was the only one! But it ticked my personal rule of less than 90 minutes travel time, I got a quick chat with former Sutton player Enzio (Boldewijn), and there was great craic seeing so many people confused at me being away from Gander Green Lane.

Lots of double takes and “are you lost?” questions. First half was excellent football-wise too… we won’t discuss the second half though.

Who was your club’s Player of the Season? Simps (Lewis Simper) won the official award, but honestly he played to the level I already expect from him, so maybe unfairly I ruled him out. My choice is Junior Eccleston.

Came through the academy and was exceptional. He played far more games than expected and looked a massive loss whenever he wasn’t in the side. Hard to believe how young he is at times.

It also helps that he’s a fantastic person off the pitch too. What was the single best moment of last season? Jack Taylor’s goal against Gateshead.

For one brief moment he identified as prime Messi ran the length of the pitch, past a few players and then slotted it home right in front of the Sutton fans. The picture was iconic. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Ollie Pearce. He scores goals. That’s what we need and what we missed at times last season.

Someone who just instinctively knows where the goal is. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager. What advice would you give him?

This is Agi, it would never be just two minutes! I’m lucky enough to speak with him fairly regularly, but seeing as I pay to watch football rather than get paid to manage it, I think any tactical advice I could offer can safely be ignored! What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

Change the layout so I can get my proper spot back! I know plenty of people have strong opinions about the ground, but every part of it has a story and its own history. Everyone at the club knows the scale of the work needed, it’s just a matter of time, money and priorities.

But if I had a magic wand, I’d redevelop the Collingwood Rec side. Add proper changing room access for the youth teams plus meeting and function rooms with external access. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

The obvious picks are the clubs who finished around the play-offs and Carlisle will probably start as favourites. But it’s not called the B****d League for nothing! With only two promotion spots available, you have to be at it constantly and summer recruitment will be massive for so many clubs.

Still, I think Carlisle just edge it. The new manager helps and if David Ajiboye rediscovers form, that could be huge. Who’ll be the surprise package?

Undoubtedly us. There are basically no expectations around Sutton again and people are slipping back into the “little old Sutton” mindset. Agi gets a full pre-season this time and now has a better understanding of how to develop the talent in the squad.

What’s one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don’t know? Piegate wasn’t - and isn’t - “great bantz”. The immediate aftermath overshadowed an incredible FA Cup run and a brilliant game against Arsenal.

Longer term, Wayne Shaw lost his livelihood and struggled badly with his mental health afterwards. But yeah… Sutton United, fat goalie, pie. Hilarious.

article.title: The Fans' View: Tamworth minds trained on historic next step
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
By this time tomorrow, the fixtures will be out and the new season will feel that much closer. There aren’t too many sets of fans who are counting down the days like they are at Tamworth - new owners have brought new life, and the club are talking up their EFL chances. All summer we have been no asking supporters for their take on the campaign just gone, and of course the one ahead.

Lambs commentator supreme Stuart Bywate r is as knowledgeable as they come. We put him on the spot to discover if this could be the club’s time to create history, and an opening day revenge mission could be in the air! Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words.

This summer has been an amazing one as a Tamworth fan, with the takeover by the DGI group finally confirmed there’s been a real buzz about transfers. My three words to describe the transfer business so far would have to be: Exciting, experience and energy. Fixture release day is tomorrow - who’s your ideal first day opponent?

It has to be Scunthorpe United at home, we faced them in our first season in the National League North at home and lost 2-1, same as last season with a home defeat by the same scoreline on opening day. It’s time for some revenge I think. What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season?

For those of you out there that don’t know, I’m the commentator for Tamworth, a job I’ve been doing for eight seasons, so grounds I’ve not been to before are a definite one I’d be looking forward too especially from a media point of view. Barrow, Harrogate, Worthing and Hornchurch are grounds I’ve never visited before, it’s really difficult to pick just one. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in Hands down it’s has to be Dan Creaney we lost him once to Solihull Moors, fortunately for us it didn’t work out there and we managed to get him back.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Honestly the only advice for Andy Peaks is have is to keep up the amazing job you’ve been doing. Morale amongst the fans wasn’t good at all before he came in.

Back to back promotions, FA Cup games against Tottenham and two county cup wins in the time he’s been at the club is just unreal. To go from the Southern Premier Central to the National League and not only just survive to compete against clubs with far bigger budgets. I just can’t wait to see what Andy can do with our new chairman’s backing.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? The pitch going back to grass for me would be massive. It would show the real intent that Tamworth want to change to get into the EFL.

The 3G surface has served us well over the years, we’ve grown as a club because of it on and off the field, but as we all know plastic in the EFL is a no-no. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Honestly I don’t know, there’s so many good teams in the National League this season it’s difficult to pick one that stands out above the rest.

It is difficult to see Barrow and Harrogate having bad seasons, also the likes of Carlisle, Boreham Wood and Southend United, who were all brilliant last season. Who’ll be the surprise package? Now I might be being slightly biased here but you honestly can’t over look Tamworth - new owners, better budgets and support from the top.

Tamworth surprised many over the last two seasons with midtable finishes. I believe that they can do one better and hit those play-offs. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

That’s a difficult one again because I’m very happy with the business Andy Peaks has done so far but if you press me I’d have to say Matt Rush from Boreham Wood, 27 goals last season can’t be overlooked. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? That the majority of us are volunteers at this level, and I have to give a massive shout out to everyone that does at their club because without volunteers we wouldn’t get to watch amazing football.

Doing commentary for the fans that can’t travel or get to games is what makes what I do so enjoyable, visiting grounds and meeting opposition media teams and seeing that we all have a real love and passion for what we do.

article.title: The Fans' View: Why Wembley could be the perfect spark for the Stones
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Wealdstone’s season was one to remember, culminating in almost 15,000 of their fans packing into Wembley Stadium. Perennially tipped to struggle, the Stones were once again having none of it in 2025/26 and a very comfortable mid-table season brings even more hope for the future. We’re asking fans of all our clubs to talk us through their season, and while there’s no doubt about the highlight for Nick DuGard , he feels life under Gary Waddock will only get better!

We’ve asked some important questions after the dust settled last Sunday. So what would he say to his manager if he could? What are his early 2026/27 predictions and what rival player would he most like to snatch?

Let’s find out. Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? Achieved beyond expectations.

What ground did you love visiting the most? I simply have to say Wembley Stadium! After our fantastic day in the FA Trophy final, after 41 years it was literally a dream that came true as, probably like many others of my age at the club, I never expected another trip to see Stones at Wembley in my lifetime.

Irrespective of the penalties it was a truly memorable occasion that was so well attended by our fans with a superb atmosphere in the National Stadium. It's second to none. Who was your club’s Player of the Season?

Has to be our goalkeeper, Dante Baptiste. Dante came into the side as pretty much an unknown a couple of seasons ago and has proved himself time and again as an ever present with crucial stops and was instrumental in our Trophy run. Has an incredibly professional attitude.

What was the single best moment of last season? Despite getting to the Trophy final, for me without doubt the most special moment was our late winning goal in the semi-final against Marine at The Vale. An unbelievably joyous moment never to be forgotten in a record breaking crowd If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Unquestionably I would sign Alex Reid. He worked wonders on loan for Wealdstone as a striker before leaving and signing for Hartlepool United. Alex was always a goal threat and scored many crucial goals for the Stones and above all was respected and loved by the fans.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? I would say to Gary Waddock simply this: "Continue to be bold in your decision making and don't be afraid to be demanding in your support expectations from the Board." But he's far to experienced to need my advice!

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? As we are planning to move to a new stadium it's virtually impossible to name one thing to change about The Vale, a ground virtually put together by the hands and sweat of our fan base. However, I would say the one thing that needs to change is our PA system!

It’s early days, but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? I have to say that Carlisle United must be favourites to win the league this coming season and will have the resources to achieve promotion as champions but once again it will be extremely competitive next campaign. Who’ll be the surprise package?

I am going to say my club, Wealdstone. Every year we are overlooked by the pundits and fans of bigger clubs and every year we surprise people. This season we have the backing of a new investor and owner who knows what we can achieve with good summer recruitment.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Back in the 1990's when Wealdstone were struggling and in administration playing in what is now Step 4 the club were desperate to move to a more cost effective regional league and in a PR stunt signed an 84-year-old called Val Shearer! It gained valuable widespread media publicity which ultimately helped the club move to a less travel onerous league, but ultimately cost us a further drop of two levels.

However, this was the start of our climb back to where we are today at Step 1 - a very long and winding road!

article.title: The Fans' View: Can the Cardinals crack it under Defoe?
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
We started last summer with Mark Hughes arriving, before Robbie Savage rolled into town at Forest Green Rovers in July. But the flow of big-name managers didn’t stop there with former England international striker Jermain Defoe five weeks before the end of the season. He has already given Woking fans plenty to be excited about - and that was before his sensational Soccer Aid double last night!

The Cardinals have already made some moves in the transfer market and Defoe appears to know exactly what he wants. We asked Woking fan Jacob Greenwood for his take on what went on last season, and what could be around the corner. Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season?

Great after February. What ground did you love visiting the most Brackley Town was a new one for me to ‘tick off’ this season so I was glad to be able to make it to that game, especially as they’ve dropped back down to the NLN now. It was a great day in the sunshine and Woking won 4-1, which doesn’t happen often!

Who was your club’s Player of the Season? I’d go with Aaron Drewe as he was dependable and surpassed expectations. After losing Dan Moss to Rochdale right-back was a key area to fill and we did that with Drewe who stepped up to playing at this level.

He was good going forwards and going backwards and, from memory, was always fit to play which is crucial. I expect him to go on to play in the Football League. What was the single best moment of last season?

After getting off to a poor start, the 5-0 home win vs Gateshead was a lot of fun. It felt like we went from being very defensive to all-out attack and it paid off. We also did ‘the double’ over Aldershot Town, so both of those games are strong contenders.

However, our 3-1 away win at Carlisle United was probably the most impressive and was my best moment, even if I couldn’t make the mid-week trip up. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? With Olly Sanderson, who contributed a lot of goals last season, as well as attacking players such as Joe Gbodé going back to their parent clubs we will need attacking reinforcements.

In a dream world Abdul Abdulmalik or someone of that style would be perfect - even if the man himself wouldn’t be realistic. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? As Jermain Defoe is inexperienced within Non-League I’d say watch as much football at this level and the National League North and South as possible as it is very different to the Premier League.

You can pick up some real gems from those leagues too, which won’t have been on his radar before getting the Woking job. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Build a new stand along the side with new facilities such as a club shop, hospitality, etc.

Everyone knows Kingfield is lopsided and the area with the dugouts currently is very old, so modernisation is required. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? It’ll be the most open league for a while next year.

Carlisle United have to be favourites for me but the pressure of that, as we saw with our 3-1 win away at their ground, can be hard to deal with. Who’ll be the surprise package? Hopefully Woking!

After last season I think a lot of people will have us down as mid-table or bottom third but hopefully we can recruit well. The manager’s pedigree is unknown but if it works out, it could put us in a great position. It feels like a long time since Darren Sarll got us into the play-offs, and I’d love another season like that.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We’ve won the FA Trophy three times and have never lost at Wembley, which included an FA Amateur Cup win in the 1950s.

article.title: The Fans' View: Rebels rising! Worthing cope with Pier pressure
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
After a few years of trying, Worthing have reached new heights - and they are planning to make the most of it. The Rebels are rising, and the club's first promotion to the top-tier of Non-League football in its 140-year history is something many fans thought they’d never see. Just over a decade ago, their team were nearly buried after £200,000 worth of debt threatened their existence.

They were rescued by 22-year-old George Dowell, who used the money he was awarded after he was left paralysed from the chest down in a car crash to transform a club on its knees into a progressive community asset. He just hoped for stability, not an ascent but dreams have come true and now they prepare to face some very big hitters just one step from the EFL. Dedicated fan Kieran Harrison was happy to talk us through an unforgettable season - and is counting down the minutes until fixture release day!

Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? Rollercoaster. Champions.

Hinsh. What ground did you love visiting the most? Dagenham & Redbridge.

Coming into the game, although they were in bad form, I thought they would bounce back with the return of Andy Carroll for his first league appearance after injury, and wasn't greatly confident coming there with our form. However, we absolutely bulldozed them 5-2 and easily could've been more. Unreal away day!

Who was your club's Player of the Season? Teddy Jenks or Joe Cook. Both carried us across so many games last year.

Teddy was unreal on several occasions with some really important goals in the middle of the season, and his on the ball talent set him apart from most opponents last season. Cooky turned up with some really important goals late on and was rock solid at the back all year. Think I'd have to edge it to Jenks though, was incredibly consistent all season.

What was the single best moment of last season? Has to be winning the league at home against Ebbsfleet. Unreal atmosphere, amazing day and long awaited.

Having suffered play-off heartbreak three seasons in a row it only felt winning the league on the last day, in front of a packed out Woodside, was poetic justice. Honourable mention to the FA Cup 4th round qualifying against Forest Green. Despite the result, the return of Adan Hinshelwood before the game was a moment that still gives me goosebumps.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Abdul Abdulmalik. Highly unrealistic but thinks he's the best player in the division by far.

Great flare, goalscorer and more than all I think he gets the crowd up with his runs down the wing. He seems to scare defenders when he runs at them, and I think partnered with Razzaq upfront at Worthing we'd be unstoppable going forward. You've got two minutes alone with your club's manager- what advice would you give him?

Carrying on with the way we play. Exciting and explosive football is what Worthing is all about and despite going up a division I think we can really go for teams this year. The players clearly have a lot of trust in Hinsh and as long as we keep the dressing room connected,I think we'll be unstoppable.

What's the one thing you would change about your team's stadium? If possible build up the Shed End being the goal. Amazing memories there but needs to be built up into a proper stand or built across the whole end of the ground.

Think it looks out of place compared to our new north stand and Elmo's end terrace.
