However, compared to our ground only a few seasons ago I couldn't ask more from George and the team and believe although it's not the biggest ground, we've definitely got some of the better facilities compared to other teams in the division, along with the best atmosphere! It's early days but who's winning the league in 2026/27?

I think Carlisle will win the league, but not convincingly. Very much think Southend could have a very good shout this year, the clear out of players so far this summer only points at some EFL replacements to finally do the job this year. Play-off glory might finally happen for them.

Who'll be the surprise package? Worthing. I think under Hinshelwood we will have a really good year, fingers crossed.

The main core of our squad - other than a couple who still need to sign on - have stayed and have really trust in the boys we've already got to do the job. I think Hinsh brings an attraction factor for young players to come to Worthing and showcase their talent, and also experienced players wishing to kick start their careers again. With a couple of additions, we can really surprise a couple of teams in this league.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Not so much about the club but the town of Worthing, we've won the Pier of the Year twice (in 2006 and 2019), which we take huge pride in. Southend now has some real competition on which team in the National League has the best Pier!

article.title: The Fans' View: Yeovil Town's shopping spree looks great value
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Not many clubs have done shopping quite like Yeovil Town this summer. A dozen new players have arrived at Huish Park but there’s no panic buys or squad fillers in sight - Billy Rowley and the Glovers mean business. Now the question on fans’ lips is if he can sculpt them into a winning side.

This close season we have asked a fan from each club to come forward and tell us why they can’t wait for the big kick-off. We put the questions to Joe Darling and it’s clear what he wants… a play-off place, an injury-free season and a few more beers to choose from! Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Looking much better.

What are your expections for next season? Play-offs minimum. I don’t want to put the pressure on, I’m not demanding promotion, but we need to be in the top seven with the investment made.

What ground are you looking forward to visiting? Hartlepool United on April 17 when we beat them to win the title! Failing that, I’ve not been to Worthing yet and I’ve heard interesting things about Hornchurch!

What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in Luke McCormick. He’s back from injury and already looking fresh. Hopefully he has a point to prove and I expect big things from him if he stays fit.

We need better luck on the injury front. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Once the season starts, calm down with the signings.

I hope I’m wrong but fear he may be one of those managers who signs two players every month if things aren’t going well. We’ve already signed 11 or 12 and it might take time. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

The selection of beers on tap. No complaints about the cider, of course. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

Hartlepool United. I’m not sure about Lee Clark, he’s not done much in a long while, but the signings they have make edge them as favourites. Who’ll be the surprise package?

We always see a promoted team do well. Two were excellent last year and Hornchurch has signed very well. Nobody will fancy it at their place.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? I don’t think there’s any point in wanting something someone else has got. I’m happy with how we are shaping up.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We dropped from the Championship to the National League South inside ten years. We went from beating Sheffield Wednesday and Nottingham Forest to losing home and away to Welling United!

A mad journey.

article.title: The Fans' View: Why Telford don't want to Buck their recent trend!
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
If, like it usually is, the remit is improving season on season, then AFC Telford fans have plenty to be proud about - and a lot to look forward to. Three years ago, the Bucks reached the Southern League play-off final but ultimately found Leamington too hard a nut to crack. A year later, the stars aligned and they reclaimed their Enterprise National League North status and went on to make the most of it - finishing in the top half and enjoying their longest FA Cup and FA Trophy runs for quite some time.

A fourth season of improvement in 2026/27 would surely see a sustained attack on the promotion places. Can Telford do it? In our latest fan review, we put the questions to New Bucks Head regular Emma Dean and here’s what she told us… Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Oli Cawthorne, re-signed!

Fixture release day is on Friday - who’s your ideal first day opponent? I'd rather play the seaside teams very early or late on in the season, so I'll go for Southport or Morecambe away. Don't really mind though, I'll just be glad to get back into it What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season?

I'm looking forward to going back to Morecambe and Hednesford. We played Morecambe away first game of the season many years ago when they joined the Conference. It was a fun day!

I am looking forward to going back to Hednesford. It's usually an exciting local fixture which would be perfect for Boxing Day. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in Oli Cawthorne was key last season and we really wanted to keep him.

Personally I fully expected him to move on but we've managed to retain him for a little longer! Which is great for the club You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Kev's not daft and I don't think he needs advice from me.

But I would reiterate that he's given us some really fun times over the last couple of seasons. And we're finally seeing some consistency in terms of player retention, which we've been missing for a few seasons now. All I ask is for a trip to Wembley, it's long overdue!

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? I'd absolutely love a Fan Zone with some beer and entertainment, and perhaps space for the younger fans to get together. Our stadium was built with EFL football in mind so doesn't have the luxury of the spare indoor space some other grounds in our division have.

We have a nice ground, but I do enjoy seeing what other clubs have to offer. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Hednesford seem to be doing alright on the money front so they ought to be in with a shot Who’ll be the surprise package?

AFC Telford! If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? I'd like to sign Ammar Dyer back from Macclesfield - he was great for us last season.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? The nearest train station to our ground is NOT Telford Central! It's Wellington.

Many fans have made that mistake over the years!

article.title: The Fans' View: Bedford pin their hopes on the exuberance of youth
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Bedford Town are putting their faith in youth next season - and we don’t just mean they’re signing up some rising stars. The Eagles have the youngest manager anywhere in senior football after appointing 28-year-old Harry Smart, who steps up from Lee Bircham’s backroom team after he left to take over at hometown club Hemel Hempstead Town. Age should be no barrier, the club say, and it seems the fans are right behind their strategy.

As we look forward to the new campaign, we continue our summer mission of speaking to a supporter from each of our member clubs. Michael Howlett is an Eyrie regular and travelled to most of the team’s away matches and he has some sound advice for the rookie manager! Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season?

I’m going to need four! Survived against all odds. What ground did you love visiting the most?

For a first season in the National League North that is really a tough choice! Especially considering the journey that Bedford Town have been on in two previous seasons. I have so many - Hereford, Chester, Macclesfield, Kidderminster, Spennymoor, Southport, AFC Fylde and South Shields.

It’s too hard to pick! Who was your club’s player of the season? Would have to be Greg Sandiford, a full-back who signed on loan from Coventry and just kept improving game by gam.

Very consistent and a real down-to-earth young lad to approach. What was the single best moment of last season? Again, it is hard to pick just one moment but in no particular order - the 1-0 win away at King’s Lynn on Easter Monday.

A 2-1 win away at Chester purely as it will go down as one of the club’s all-time great league wins and South Shields away as a full trip for weekend in Newcastle! If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? I would say in four different areas so four different types of signing, firstly I would say Luca Miller who I believe he is still at Peterborough Sports but destroyed us single handedly last season when we lost 3-1 in away game.

Paul Dawson from Macclesfield, a proper winner and influence in central midfield. Matty Stenson from AFC Telford is a pure goalscorer, and finally either Rory McCauley or Liam Dolman from Harborough Town. Both would add a lot of needed experience to our back line.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? You have been there as part of the backroom staff and enjoyed it, now embrace the challenge of being Bedford Town manager. You will be backed on your whole journey.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Maybe the usual renovation, like a better away supporters area and a general increase of the capacity but other than that, I really wouldn't change the Eyrie for anything! It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

For my early predictions I would say either Macclesfield, South Shields, or Brackley Town. Who’ll be the surprise package? I think after all of their troubles last season then I would say Hereford or Southport have a great chance of shocking a few!

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We were a club with good FA Cup pedigree back in the 50s and 60s with several notable scalps, also in 24/25 season we were a few months away from not existing as a football club and being taken over by our next-door neighbours.

article.title: The Fans' View: Brackley have the tools for the restoration job
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
After the collapse comes the restoration job. That’s what Brackley Town fans are hoping with just three to go until their National League North return begins. Their first season at the top table was going perfectly to plan before Shrewsbury Town came knocking for their manager Gavin Cowan.

Although Andy Whing has an impressive CV, he wasn’t able to halt a terrible two month tumble that ultimately saw the Saints swallowed up. But an impressive summer of recruitment hints at a total reset. We asked supporter Charlie Covacic-Field to talk us through turning a negative into a positive.

Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Young exciting talents. What are your expections for next season - and can they be achieved? I’m really hoping we can compete with a strong manager and a strong foundation of a squad.

I can see us maybe getting the play-offs if we start the season well and our squad gels quickly enough. What ground are you looking forward to visiting? Hednesford is definitely one of the top ones on the list, it’s a crazy ground for this level.

Also have to say Macclesfield is up there too! What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in? That would have been Morgan Roberts if he stayed but from the current crop, Kyle Morrison is definitely the one.

So solid at the back and will be able to help the new lads settle in nicely. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? First thing is to keep the fans close to you.

The fans are a massive part of the club and having a gaffer that supports that helps us out loads. Having chats with Whingy, he seems good and he’s a nice chap. Also, just keep us believing.

This club has caused so many upsets over the years and we don’t want to stop that. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Make the away end see-through so I can watch the games from the cricket pitch behind while I’m playing!

Also to get Jubel on tap, unreal beer. It’s early days, but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? I would honestly have to say Oxford City.

They’ve recruited so well, including a couple of players from us from last year. They’ve got a gaffer that’s used to winning. Who’ll be the surprise package?

The surprise package I can see is AFC Telford. Their fans seem to be a bit down but keeping Remi Walker and Matt Stenson is massive! I really rate Remi as a player!

Also Kev (Wilkin) is a great manager and plays simple football that works so well. They’ll be up there for me. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

I’ve mentioned him before, but Remi Walker. He’s a top lad with a great way about him. He’s been absolutely unreal for Telford and is still only young.

I think he would’ve been great in our midfield. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? One thing that other clubs don’t know about us… probably that we are so, so close to all the people from the club.

Everyone seems to know each other and we always have had a close relationship with managers and players. Often players are spending free time with fans and enjoy sitting down and chatting to us!

article.title: The Fans' View: Buxton boxing clever as they try to build on historic season
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
A new era is now underway at Buxton following Friday’s new manager announcement. Jordan Broadbent is the man picked to replace FC Halifax Town-bound John McGrath - and he has got a lot to live up to. The Bucks bar is at its highest having just recorded the club’s best-even league finish, and back-to-back Enterprise National League North play-off placements.

You can understand why supporters are keen to remember a history-making campaign as they begin to look to the future at Silverlands. Sam Longden knows the success of outgoing McGrath proves experience in the division isn’t the be-all-and-end-all. We put the important questions to him in our latest fan review following an important few days.

Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? Highest ever finish. What ground did you love visiting the most Penydarren Park, home of Merthyr Town.

We played Merthyr at our place back in 2022 in the FA Cup first round, so I was really keen to visit their ground. The staff and fans were really welcoming, and it was great to see all the flags and banners steeped in history - such their famous win at home to Atalanta. It helped that the Bucks had a convincing win to kick-start our late play-off chase.

Who was your club’s Player of the Season? For me it would be Connor Kirby, the captain. Kirbs made his 200th appearance for the Bucks this season, and it’s arguably been his best in a Buxton shirt.

He’s a great footballer, really passionate, controls the midfield well, and chips in with some great goals too - he doesn’t score tap-ins, only bangers! He rarely misses a game either and is always a reliable, consistent player. Connor’s also a great lad off the pitch and has a good connection with the fans and volunteers around the Club.

What was the single best moment of last season? Our incredible play-off victory over Scarborough Athletic. I don’t think I’ve enjoyed a game quite like that in a while - it was incredible, and the lads played out of their skin.

I’ve watched the goals back several times. The Bucks recorded their highest ever league finish this season, followed by going one better in the play-offs with that win. It felt like there was a real buzz about town leading into that game too, and the performance on the night was superb.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? I think it’s safe to say every team is looking for a consistent goal scorer. I’d love to see Rio Clegg swap Radcliffe blue for Bucks’ blue.

He works hard on and off the ball, brings plenty of energy, and certainly has an eye for goal. He’s definitely someone I enjoy watching when we play against the Boro. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

The Bucks have just announced Jordan Broadbent as our new manager. He’s got some great experience coming in from Sheffield Wednesday. He looks like a fresh, exciting appointment.

I’m really pleased. If I had two minutes with him, I’d say Buxton is a really great place and a really tight-knit club. The fans and community will really appreciate anyone who is willing to get stuck in across the club - so my advice to the incoming manager would be just that: get involved.

Speak to fans, chat with players in our youth system, and be present around the club. The “Railway Enders” and the fans will give you all the support in return. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

This is an interesting question, because there are some big changes already planned at the Tarmac Silverlands Stadium! There are plans for a new main stand which will add an extra 500 seats, with new sponsors/director facilities, club shop, and changing rooms. I think adding some seats and a cover to the “allotment end” would really round the ground off nicely too.

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? I think Morecambe might be favourites if they can steady the ship. They’ve been through a real torrid period and I feel for the fans but this season could be the start of their revival.

I also think South Shields will be in the fight again after missing out on play-off promotion. It sounds like they’ve secured some good additional investment too so they could have more to spend. Who’ll be the surprise package?

I think Oxford City are going to be good this season. They’ve already signed Tyrone Marsh from Bedford Town, who will add plenty of goals, and brought in Jonny Maxted at the other end. It’ll be interesting to see who else they sign through the summer.

I wouldn’t rule out one or two of the newly promoted sides having a good run either - Hednesford look like a club with big ambitions. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? The Tarmac Silverlands Stadium is the highest ground in England at 1,020ft!

At times, it can be the wettest and windiest ground too - as seen in our televised FA Cup game against Morecambe a couple of years ago!

article.title: The Fans' View: Park life! Chester have had their Phil of near-misses
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
It comes to something when Chester fans are so excited by their new manager that they are willing to turn a blind eye to the fact he has the same name as Wrexham’s! Well, they do say if you can't beat them, join them. Phil Parkinson returned to football early this summer and they are looking to secure promotion back to the National League after eight years away.

He told supporters they should expect a “real modern-day approach to football” - and the Deva Stadium faithful just want it to be a winning one. Seals superfan Matt Irwin was put on the spot in our latest fan view feature with the countdown to the first day of the season on! Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Good solid signings.

What are your expectations for next season - and can they be achieved? Phil Parkinson is an experienced, quality manager and based on the mix of young hungry players and the experienced heads he has brought in I would say play-offs are attainable. What ground are you looking forward to visiting?

I will be looking to do a few new grounds next season Hebburn, Spalding and Harborough....best away day on paper is Morecambe local game good away following on a Saturday. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in Difficult one as we have had wholesale changes, but, when fit and firing Jack Bainbridge is usually superb for us.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? This would probably be to block out the noise of X, Facebook and the forum Deva Chat due to the ridiculous nature of the over the top comments whether we win, lose or draw. From what I've seen and heard so far he gets the club the way it is run and the passion for it What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

Some very good friends of mine have raised money for a viewing gallery for those less able so I would love to see that come to life. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Based on summer signings and budget I would go for Macclesfield Who’ll be the surprise package?

Possibly one of the more southern based teams that have been promoted! If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Paul Blackett from South Shields.

A proper player and a proper goal scorer. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We once had a player score 73 goals in a single season, Arthur Gale.

article.title: The Fans' View: No play-offs this time, but enough pleasure for Chorley
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
After two play-off finishes in consecutive seasons, expectation was again high at Chorley. Andy Preece’s team were hoping to take the next step after racking up 79 points in 2025/26, and 83 the year before. But in football things don’t always go to plan - and as Pete Tscherewik explains, sometimes that’s OK.

The Magpies eventually finished 15th in the Enterprise National League North and by their own standards didn’t quite hit the heights of years gone by. In the latest in our series of summer features, the Chorley fan says there were still plenty of positives to take with more firm foundations laid for the future. Here, Pete looks at the campaign gone, the one to come and picks the dream player he would sign if he could over the next few months!

Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? A minor blip. What ground did you love visiting the most It has to be Penydarren Park, the home of Merthyr Town, for me.

As a proud Welshman myself, it's a fairly predictable pick, but I think not only that, if you'd have told me that Chorley would have played domestic football against a team in Wales back when I became involved with the club back in 2018/19, I'd have said there's no way! A lovely ground, a lovely group of people and supporters, and winning in the last kick of the game was all the more sweeter, especially for the coach trip back to Lancashire! Who was your club’s Player of the Season?

I'd go for Warren Clarke. Warren scooped a good few of the clubs' official awards, but, despite that, I've always had Warren as a steady, an 8/10 every week, Mr. Consistent if you like.

A utility player with bags of energy and tenacity was definitely the standout for me over the course of the 46-game season. What was the single best moment of last season? Beating Macclesfield away in the final minute of the game.

A free-kick from Jack Moore, off the underside of the crossbar, off the goalkeeper then out to Mike Calveley to prod it home from close range in front of the away end. Absolute pandemonium, right next to the travelling supporters, a moment I got very, very excited over, when doing live commentary of the game. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

One player that instantly springs to mind is Paul Blackett. Pace, power, and ultimately, firepower in front of goal. For me, the best number nine in the league and ultimately, he brings a certain aura about him, teams instantly think they're up against it when he's in the starting eleven and I think he would be the ultimate striker to work off of Jack Sampson for Chorley.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Keep doing what you're doing. The amount of work that goes on behind the scenes is unprecedented, the attention to detail.

everything is done to an absolute tee. Andy Preece has overachieved as Chorley manager year on year, with the 2025/26 the only exception. People forget about how good a job he, his staff and the players have done for the club over the years.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? I'd like a scoreboard, it's a strange one to pinpoint but it's sometimes finicky to have to rely on different devices as time-keeping during the game. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

South Shields for me. I think they'll strengthen again this summer and come out firing, this time, with Promotion Final disappointment behind them, and be able to go one better and lift the title next year. Who’ll be the surprise package?

A left-field shout, but, Oxford City. They've already secured two fantastic additions in Tyrone Marsh and Jonny Maxted. A proven forward, and an experienced goalkeeper.

Having struggled in the last two seasons, I'd back them as a full-time outfit to bounce-back better in 2026/27. They might not end up right at the top-end of the table but I'd definitely expect a fair bit of improvement under Ross Jenkins next season. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

Vitinha, now a back-to-back Champions League winner with PSG, scored the winner for Wolves at Victory Park in the fourth round of the FA Cup against Chorley in January 2021. A 0-1 win for Nuno Espirito Santo's side, a superb strike from 35-yards, a period where Vitinha was struggling to get in their team.

article.title: The Fans' View: How the supporters are still supercharging Darlington
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
It might be becoming more and more difficult, but Darlington are continuing to show you can flourish being fan run in 2026. As football at all levels becomes increasingly demanding financially, the Quakers are operated solely by their supporters - relying on what the club brings in to fund on-the-field operations. They've already rasied almost £200,000 this summer to help manager Steve Watson's charge next time.

They are one of the few trust run clubs in the country, so their play-off near miss in April may have hurt even more. A ninth-place finish last term has raised hopes they can go one stage further when the 2026/27 season kicks off in under two months, especially with some extra budget to play with. Super fan Paul Moss answered our questions and says firm foundations have been put in place.

Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? Building towards something What ground did you love visiting the most? South Shields, we have a good record there in recent seasons, and it’s always a good atmosphere.

Who was your club’s Player of the Season? Will McGowan would be my pick for player of the season, a standout year which has deservedly earned him a move upwards. What was the single best moment of last season?

Probably the 4-0 demolition of Spennymoor at The Brewery Field, we were excellent that day and they couldn’t lay a glove on us. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? For me it would have to be Paul Blackett from South Shields, guaranteed goals.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Great question, but a really difficult one to answer. It’s clear that both he and our assistant Terry Mitchell work really hard, so my message would be simply to keep building and progressing as we are getting close to being a very good team that can challenge.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? It would have to be our pitch, with it being a shared surface it’s not always as we would want it to be for flowing football. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

It’s probably hard to look too far past Morecambe, but I’d say one of either Morecambe, Macclesfield or Brackley Town. Who’ll be the surprise package? Hereford.

They struggled last year but I can see them having a much better year. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We are 100 per cent owned by our supporters.

article.title: Welcome to the Enterprise National League North: Harborough Town
article.author: Tom Scott
article.html:
Here is the lowdown on Enterprise National League North Harborough Town ahead of the new season. Factfile Last Season: Southern League Central - Champions Top Scorer: Riley O’Sullivan (17) Manager: Mitch Austin Ground: Harborough Town Community Football Ground Best National League Performance: N/A How they got here... Harborough Town were formed as a youth football club in 1975 – but since merging with adult side Spencer United in 2008, their trajectory has been steep.

They enjoyed 119 goals in a single United Counties League season in 2021-22, a play-off promotion from the Northern Premier League despite a six-point deduction in 2023-24, and then an FA Cup second-round appearance in their very first Southern League campaign, losing a breathless eight-goal thriller at League One Reading after extra time. Their second season at Step 3 went even better – just three league defeats all year, and an FA Cup fourth round qualifying tie at National League side Altrincham which produced one of the stories of the round… 2-0 down with three minutes to play, they hauled themselves level and forced a replay at the Beehive, where a club-record crowd of 1,813 watched them hold firm with ten men for nearly 100 minutes before Altrincham's quality told in extra time. The title was confirmed on 11 April with a 3-1 comeback win at Halesowen – a third promotion in five seasons, and the first time a Leicestershire club has reached Step 2 since Hinckley United in 2013.

Their first appearance as a National League club. Keep an eye out for... The Bees have made a few exciting signings this season but midfielder Prince Mancinelli is definitely one to watch.

Moving to the club from Barwell, the powerhouse midfielder could be just what they’re looking for in their first season at Step 2. Main image - Brandon Hallmark

article.title: Welcome to the Enterprise National League North: Hebburn Town
article.author: Tom Scott and Richard Dorman
article.html:
Here is the lowdown on Enterprise National League North Hebburn Town ahead of the new season. Factfile Last Season: Northern Premier League - Champions Top Scorer: Gary Martin (26) Manager: Daniel Moore Ground: The Trustmark Group Stadium Best National League Performance: N/A How they got here... While neighbours Newcastle United spend hundreds of millions a few miles up the road, Hebburn Town were fighting for survival less than a decade ago – crowds below 30, the club’s future genuinely in doubt.

An emergency appeal from then-manager Scott Oliver sparked a revival that has never really stopped: an FA Vase final at Wembley in 2021, won 3-2 against Consett through substitute Olly Martin’s late goal, and a steady climb through the pyramid under current boss Daniel Moore. A Division One East title in 2023-24 earned them a place in the Premier Division of the Northern Premier League – where they were promptly installed as relegation favourites. They lost their first three.

As Moore recalled: “I think someone said to me we were 250/1 to win the league after those games – and I think that probably sums us up to be honest with you.” What followed was one of the stories of the non-league season: W23 D10 L7, 75 goals scored, 41 conceded – with just one home defeat all season, on the opening day. The home crowd which you could count by eye a decade ago had grown to 397 on the opening day of the season and continued to grow towards the crescendo of a club-record 3,000 who flocked to see a title-clinching final-day win against Rushall Olympic on 25 April.

The Hornets join the National League ranks for the first time. Keep an eye out for... Midfielder Liam Murray has gone from strength to strength since signing his first senior contract with the club back in 2022.

After bagging two of the club’s Player of the Year awards for his efforts last season, don’t be surprised to see his incredible rise continue in the Enterprise National League North. Main Image - Tyler's Mission

article.title: Welcome to the Enterprise National League North: Hednesford Town
article.author: Tom Scott and Richard Dorman
article.html:
Here is the lowdown on Enterprise National League North Hednesford Town ahead of the new season. Factfile Last Season: Northern Premier League – Play-Off Final winners Top Scorer: Akheem Rose (13) Manager: Kelvin Davis Ground: Keys Park Best National League Performance: 3rd – National League (1995/96) How they got here... Hednesford Town – the Pitmen – are no strangers to this level.

They spent six seasons in the Conference between 1995 and 2001, reached the FA Cup fourth round in 1996-97 defeating Blackpool and York City before losing to Middlesbrough, and won the FA Trophy in 2004 by beating Canvey Island 3-2 at Villa Park. A second stint in the Conference North followed from 2013 to 2016. Then came a slide that nearly ended the club entirely: relegation to Step 4 in 2023, a collapsed takeover, and a fan-led rescue that kept them alive.

Two promotions in two seasons brought them back to the NPL Premier for 2025-26, and they wasted little time reasserting themselves. The visit of FC United of Manchester to Keys Park on Boxing Day drew a ground record of 4,784 supporters. Stockton Town were vanquished 2-0 in the play-off semi-final; they had to dig deep to find a 90th-minute leveller in the final against Warrington Rylands to send the fixture into extra time.

30 minutes more couldn’t divide the sides as Hednesford won 5-4 on penalties. The Pitmen are back. Keep an eye out for...

One of a few eye-catching signings so far this summer has shown that the Pitmen mean business. The capture of flying winger Dylan Mottley-Henry from Chester is a great signing.

article.title: The Fans' View: Why Downes has Hereford looking up again
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
They may have had games in hand, but plenty of managers would have shuddered at the thought of performing a rescue act at a club 11 points from safety with two months to go. Talk about throwing yourself in at the deep end. Aaron Downes had been an assistant for the best part of a decade and was “waiting for the right opportunity” to become a number one.

Hereford were happy he applied. The club successfully dodged relegation from the Enterprise National League with a late-season surge playing twice a week, safety sealed on a nail-biting final day. But as fun as it all was, he doesn’t fancy having to do it all again.

The Bulls are hoping for much better next season, and supporter Matt Hale has explained why optimism has grown despite an almost devastating season. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Exciting, promising, correcting. Fixture release day is on Friday July 10 - who’s your ideal first day opponent?

There is never a perfect start to a season fixture wise. But for Hereford this season a home game to start would be huge. Someone like Worksop or Bedford at home is as close as it would get to ideal for me.

What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season? There are some amazing grounds at the level this season. But the one that I really cannot wait for is Hednesford!

A gorgeous stadium that has undergone huge upgrades since my last visit. Will be a top day out. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in If I had been writing this a couple of weeks ago I would have been begging for a Aaron Skinner contract extension...

and luckily enough my prayers came through and we got the news! But still we can't lose our starman. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

I would tell him to keep doing everything he is doing and stay confident. Aaron and Harry [Pell] have been excellent because they are confident with the players and the players show it back. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

I would love us to build the new Blackfriars End stand. This has not been in use for a very very long time and got demolished a couple of years ago. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

It will be one of the most competitive league seasons in recent times, the obvious answer is Morcambe but as Scunthorpe United showed a few years ago it is not as easy as it looks. Hednesford look very strong as do South Shields, but if I had to pick one it would be Hednesford, simply off their early summer business. Who’ll be the surprise package?

I think we will be a fairly big surprise to some after a poor season last season. A big push for top seven could follow - very optimistic I know! Hebburn Town are also looking strong to maybe shock a few.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Lewys Twamley at Merthyr Town. He is just unreal and has the stats to back it.

Unfortunately, he has just moved to Southend! What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? The meadow End at Edgar Street is curved due to the ground formerly having a running track around it.

article.title: The Fans' View: 'I'm hoping to capture some big King's Lynn Town moments!'
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
He may only be 16, but there’s not much King’s Lynn Town fan Liam Tompson-Whyte doesn’t know about the Enterprise National League North. Going around the grounds capturing the atmosphere and big moments for his popular YouTube channel Travelling TW , the young fan has built-up a following of thousands as he hits the road with his dad. We are clearly in good hands as we ask the teenager to talk us through the up-coming season, Lynn’s chances and for his bold promotion predictions.

As Liam took time out plotting where he’s heading to for the first few weeks of the new season, we grilled him on what’s in store for Paul Caddis’ team ahead of 2026/27. The new campaign is little over a week away now - so what can we expect come kick-off? Sum up your club’s summer so far in just three words Exciting, positive, united.

What are your expectations for next season - and are they realistic? Next season I am hoping for an improved finish on last year’s 19th place. For me there have been many player movements from when Adam Lakeland got a play-off finish with the Linnets so with Paul Caddis now as manager and more time with the squad I will be happy with a mid-table finish, let’s say 13th.

What ground are you looking forward to visiting? Merthyr Town has always caught my eye, or more like my eye for food. The Merthyr sausage and chips in a cob drowned in curry sauce looks delicious, so Merthyr is on my list purely for the scran.

However, I would also like to get down to Hednesford Town as their new modern stadium is definitely one to visit. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in? If you asked me this a couple months ago I would’ve said Morgan Williams but Harrogate Town have snapped him up, so for me I’m going to say Ross Crane.

A tricky winger, who last season was a valuable reason to why Lynn stayed up with his 13 goals and 10 assists. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? The fans are back on your side, you proved everyone wrong before by keeping this team in the division so prove them wrong again.

Give the fans football that is a joy to watch as this squad has the talent to do so. Push for a better finish (promotion would be nice) and get the strikers scoring some goals! What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

The main stand seats covered in tape, making the stand look like a crime scene It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? While I’d love to be biased and say King’s Lynn, being realistic I think Macclesfield will win this division. Last season they caused a huge upset against Crystal Palace in the FA Cup and went on to get into the play-offs.

This season I think they will improve on that and win the division but will be challenged by the likes of Morecambe and Chester. Who’ll be the surprise package? This is something I am almost certain will happen (it may come back to bite me) but Oxford City will be a completely different side from their previous relegation-fighting seasons.

They finished last season on good form and have signed many good additions like Tyrone Marsh, Scott Pollock and Ellis Brown, all players proven at the level. I would also say Spalding United are definitely going to go under the radar as a newly promoted side they are looking very solid for the 26/27 season. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Paul Blackett from South Shields, the top scorer last season with 29 goals and he consistently is hitting high scoring figures. This would massively help a side like King’s Lynn but I don’t think Blackett would fancy the four hour journey from Tyneside to Norfolk. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

That Michael Clunan, who is current club captain and a player, is currently taking on the role of Chief Executive, combining both playing with a football administration role and not to forget we have the best commentator in the league with Noah Crowe!

article.title: The Fans' View: Now sensational Silkmen just want promotion!
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Dreaming big ahead of kick-off in just over three weeks time? One club last season taught everyone that anything is genuinely possible - but this time it’s all about promotion for Macclesfield. They club created worldwide headlines when they sent FA Cup holders Crystal Palace packing, one of the greatest upsets ever in the famous competition.

They couldn’t quite do the double by winning the Enterprise National League North play-offs, but they want another crack at it. We asked Silkmen superfan Owen Banks to fill us in on the club’s summer so far, and he selected the sides who he predicts will also be battling for the title with them. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words It's very ambitious.

What are your expectations for next season - and can they be achieved? Based on the business in the window other clubs have done, I think it'll be a very difficult season but I think we will comfortably finish in the play-offs again. I think based on last season this target is very realistic.

What ground are you looking forward to visiting? There are a couple of grounds I would like to go to next season, including some of the new ones - but I would really like to go to Morecambe's ground. They were only in League One about four years ago or more, so that is the ground I'd love to visit.

What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in The player I'd hate to see get for any money would definitely be Paul Dawson. It would feel season-ending if he left, but it obviously wouldn't be. It would be devastating to see him leave.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? If I could speak to John Rooney for a few minutes, I would tell him to tell the players not to be out of position and to sign a new number 9. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

I would add a roof to the open standing terrace opposite the Star Lane end. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? It’s between four clubs.

I think the title contenders will be Macc, Morecambe, South Shields and maybe even Hednesford. Who’ll be the surprise package? I think Hednesford will be the team to watch this upcoming season.

I've been looking at the signings they've made and they look strong. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? I would have said Alex Curran from Curzon Ashton but they unfortunately got relegated last season so I am going to say Dylan Mottley-Henry from Hednesford.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? One thing that most other fans wouldn't know is the Macc were the last team to score a goal in the English Leagues before the turn of the millennium.

article.title: The Fans' View: Marine keep moving in spite of Wembley agony
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Despite knowing they did so well to get there, being able to reach out and almost touch Wembley still leaves Marine fans sore. They were a stone's throw from the national stadium in more ways that one in April, falling just short in their semi-final at Wealdstone where they got a heartbreaking glimpse of the nearby national stadium on their way home. Agony for sure, but the hurt couldn't mask another season of improvement after a top half finish, ending four points and three places better off than in 2025/26.

They are the latest subject of our Fans' View - asking the dedicated supporters some vital, and maybe not so important, questions about this season and next. Marine regular Thomas Kayll is on the spot - let's see what he has come up with. Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season?

Gritty team effort. What ground did you love visiting the most? I’d have to say our home stadium.

There’s no place like home especially when it has such a sense of community. It’s a great all round matchday experience at Rossett Park. Who was your club’s Player of the Season?

Adam Thomas. The type of bloke you’d like to have with you in the trenches, will put his hand up to play anywhere and never puts a foot wrong. What was the single best moment of last season?

Probably beating Tamworth on penalties in the FA Trophy. We ended up falling short in the semi-final, but it was the day supporters could seriously start dreaming of a Wembley trip for the first time in the club's history. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Charlie Jolley, who's been released by Fylde. He was excellent for us on loan last season. Luke Brennan at Buxton is also a wonderful footballer.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? I'd just tell Bobby Grant to keep doing what he is doing. He's got a group of lads who will run through brick walls for the club and for a part time club he's done superbly well to drill this identity into the group.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Better music playlists on a matchday. Go more towards upcoming artists in the city and show off the array of talent that there is.

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? As much as I would love to say Marine, I have a suspicion that Macclesfield will be champions. They were the best side that came to Marine last season and I was shocked that they never went up in the play-offs.

Who’ll be the surprise package? I think this actually could be Marine. I think if we were luckier with injuries last season we would've been close to a playoff place.

We've already retained some excellent talent and with Bobby Grant's links I have full confidence we will strengthen the group even more. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Borussia Dortmund trained at Marine on the day they lost to Liverpool in 2016, there is a signed shirt from Sokratis inside the boardroom from that day.

article.title: The Fans' View: Here's how Morecambe turn around the tumble down the divisions
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Since their formation back in 1920, Morecambe were notable for not experiencing a single relegation from any league they played in until 2023. They do say all good things have to come to an end, but three in four years? That's some punishment for the Shrimps fans.

A tumble has turned to free-wheeling through the divisions. Three years ago playing in League One, the club now set up camp in the Enterprise National League North. But they arrive with genuine hope that a reversal of fortune is approaching.

Adam Lakeland has been lured from FC Halifax to lead the charge, while a squad of pedigree is being put into place. Super fan Liam Withers is expectant - and wants to buck the recent trend by looking up instead of down. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Refreshing, ambitious and intent.

Fixture release day is on Friday July 10 - who’s your ideal first day opponent? Macclesfield at home would be nice, two big clubs at the level locking horns .... The feel of both fan bases on social media suggests they both think the league is theirs to lose.

It would be a bumper crowd and also saves the likes of Southport, Chester and Chorley for the festive/bank holiday fixtures! What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season? Probably two.

First is Marine. That’s a proper Non-League set-up that has been their home since the turn of the 1900's and the other is Chorley - similar reasons but they also have a great fan experience/set up socially and even host away sides higher up then Pyramid when playing in the surrounding areas. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in For me I'm not that precious over any of them from last year.

Jack Nolan was the obvious one but he's already rightly gone to Hartlepool, with Miguel Azeez to Carlisle too. I would like us to keep Lewis Payne who we've yet to hear about as he was one of a few players who really dug in last year after Jim Bentley came back. He'd be quality at this level.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Engage with the fans, don't think we are just another group who will want you out when things get tough. We've suffered in silence for too long and just want to know what's going on.

We will back a dead horse if we feel part of the journey. Be open in interviews and always show appreciation to the crowd. Before Jim last year, that was a huge problem for us.

Nice, fluent and tidy and attacking football would be nice but it’s about effort first. We have to throw everything at winning this league first time. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

It's a great ground for the level obviously but it needs some coverage on the 'Berlin Wall' side. I would also like to see them open behind the 'away' goal for home fans when the crowds for the away team don't come in numbers, allowing us to swap ends at half-time. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

Genuinely believe it will be Morecambe. If I'm not allowed to pick my own team, I think Phil Parkinson will get a tune out of Chester and they've signed some good players at this level. Who’ll be the surprise package?

Spennymoor Town, pushing for the play-offs. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Paul Blackett at South Shields.

Just a goalscorer! Loves it. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

From our formation in 1920 until the end of the 2022–23 season, every league change we experienced was either a promotion or a restructuring of the football Pyramid. We had never finished a season and been relegated. When twe stayed up in League One in 2021–22, we were believed to be the only club in England's top four divisions that had never suffered relegation ...

How that record quickly undid itself! However we are on the up again, hopefully.

article.title: The Fans' View: Are Oxford City one of the dark horses?
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
If you’re hunting for an outside tip for success next season, you may want to look in the direction of Oxford City. Some shrewd summer signings, a really strong ended to 2025/26 and a manager who knows what it takes to get the club up. There’s certainly a buzz around Court Place Farm again.

Not that Ross Jenkins wouldn’t probably prefer staying totally under the radar as he plots significant improvement after a 17th place finish. Supporter Alfie Greenwood is used to clocking up the miles to watch City in action and is more excited about a season than he has been for some time. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words.

Ambition being shown. What are the expectations at Oxford City next season - and what can be achieved? With the signings we have made so far, I think promotion is definitely the aim.

If we carry our brilliant form from the back end of last season into this one, I think it’s definitely possible. What ground are you looking forward to visiting? Brackley away!

Close compared to some of the other journeys in this league and should have a good atmosphere. Considering it’s a bit of a derby, maybe a bit of stick shared between both home and away supporters. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in.

It’s got to be Zac McEachran - been at the club since 2017 and has made himself a club legend. 287 appearances, 52 goals and 17 assists at attacking midfield says all you need to know. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

I’d say try to make sure that there are no issues with squad depth before the start of the season because that’s one of the main issues we’ve had in the past. In this league, especially with all the travelling we have to do, fatigue is a huge factor. We were plagued with injuries for a lot of last season and didn’t really have the depth to deal with it.

So I’d say to Ross just bring in some good players from lower levels who are willing to be impact subs or backups to reduce the impact of injuries. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? I would say a new digital scoreboard.

Every time we have opposition fans or even new fans come to our ground, the first thing they often mention is that our current scoreboard needs fixing. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? The Enterprise National League North this season is probably the toughest it’s ever been, but I have to say Morecambe.

The signings they’ve made so far look fantastic and with Adam Lakeland in charge, I can only see them winning the league by a distance. Who’ll be the surprise package? I honestly think we will be the suprise package this season.

City have really gone under the radar this window: signing the third top scorer in the league last season Tyrone Marsh. We have also added experienced National League players in Scott Pollock, Jonny Maxted, Dejan Tetek and Ludwig Francilette - plus 2 up and coming talents in Ellis Brown and Keegan Bloom. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

I’d probably go for Macclesfield’s Paul Dawson. I think his leadership and experience is what every club at this level needs and he’s a fantastic player. He obviously scored that goal against Crystal Palace which is a great achievement.

But for a defensive midfielder, scoring 12 goals and being Macc’s top goalscorer last season is incredibly impressive. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Not a lot of people know that we were once managed by England World Cup winner Bobby Moore and that his assistant was Harry Redknapp.

article.title: The Fans' View: Radcliffe hope Rio and co are ready for more!
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
While this time of the year is always packed full of excitement about players fans want to sign, Radcliffe supporters are just hoping they keep hold of some of their big hitters. In Rio Clegg, who shone last season after stepping up after signing from Trafford, they have a player who has quickly become a cult hero. We are cracking on with our close season mega mission - speaking to a supporter at every club, getting their views on the season gone, the one ahead and what advice they would give their manager!

We’re asking each of the fans the same ten questions as we find out a little more about what makes their club so special. Radcliffe supporter Ryan Lewis lend us some of his time to talk about the Boro... and there was no surprise to hear his biggest summer wish!

Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Younger, sharper, unfinished. Fixture release day is on Friday July 10 - who’s your ideal first day opponent? I’m going to say Morecambe or Scarborough, maybe Marine at a pinch… very little to do with the football, we’ve got to play everyone at some point any way so might as well throw in a nice beach trip with the family before the football whilst the weather is more likely to be on our side!

What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season? Merthyr. It’s a long old trip, but I really enjoyed it last year.

A great old ground, good food, the gaffer bought us a pint after the game, and quite a few stayed for a good night out and made the most of it on the back of a great 5-0 away win. No reason to think it wouldn’t be exactly the same this time around, right? What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in?

It’s hard to look anywhere but one place - National League North player of the month twice, cleaned up at the club awards do, one that keeps cropping up when anyone is mentioning who they’d want to pick up from ourselves or even the league as a whole. Sometimes you’re not sure if even Rio Clegg knows quite what he’s going to do next, but he’s certainly a right handful when he’s on his game! You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

Genuinely, what could I say that’s worth saying? Bernard is a local lad, played for the club, gets what it’s about really and there’s not many out there with his track record around over the years either is there? To be fair to all the management – they’re not shy in coming to Friends of the Boro meetings and having an honest conversation, so - boring answer I know - but he’s got backing if he’s any reason to even think not, be brave and go for it.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Genuinely - this is where a time machine would be helpful - knock me back 60 years and just move it over enough to give space to develop it properly on the grounds we have rather than being pinned into the corner with no drainage up there, the houses and the lodge backing on. Assuming the budget won’t stretch to that - it’d be nice to hear the tannoy down the far side, and generally just a bit more noise all over!

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? It’s hard to look past Macclesfield or Morecambe. There’s some big clubs in this division but they’re both among those with most pedigree and have made some eye catching signings so far.

Who’ll be the surprise package? I’d say Harborough Town might be one some are sleeping on - not one of the bigger names, freshly promoted… I’m not going to say they’ll tear the whole league up but we went down for pre-season the year we won the NPL and they had a good side, and a ground where they can make it tough for you that’s for sure. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

It would have to be a midfielder, I'd be honest, that’s where we look lightest. I'm not one who knows extensively about other clubs and their players, I'm a Boro fan so I'm hoping the scouts know better than me - but Kian Scales looked decent when with us at the back end of last year, so lets go for him. Buxton have themselves a good one there.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We’re little old Radcliffe right, so there’s probably loads… the most common ‘surprising’ things about the club are the links with Bernard Manning and that some big names have turned out for us over the years (Gazza, Lee Sharpe Frank Worthington, Peter Barnes, Gordon Hill, Alan Kennedy, Len Cantello) and a couple of other Premier League players (Craig Dawson, Darren Sheridan) started out with the club. So if we skip over them - something maybe even some of our own fans don’t know - Radcliffe JFC Foundation is recognised as the North West's largest grassroots football club with over 1,000 players and 70 teams.

It’s not the headline and glamour side of things, but it’s pretty impressive!

article.title: The Fans' View: The exiled Seadogs of Scarborough didn't lack bite!
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
When you’ve got one of Manchester United’s treble winners leading you forward, it’s understandable to think anything is possible. But even when you’ve been forced to move out of your new stadium, playing your home games 20 miles away in Bridlington? Nothing’s impossible at Scarborough Athletic.

Tipped by some to really struggle, the Seadogs didn’t lack bite and made the Enterprise National League play-offs before their fantastic odds-defying season came to end in the Eliminator against Buxton. Manager Jonathan Greening brought the belief back despite every match being like an away game. It has fallen to Curt from the Seadogs On Tour YouTube channel to talk us through a campaign that is sure to live long in the memory with a record points haul posted in Greening's fifth year at the helm.

So what was his favourite moment? What are the early 2026/27 predictions and what rival player would he most like to get his hands on? Let’s find out.

Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? Against all odds. What ground did you love visiting the most?

I didn’t manage to get there last season, but I always enjoy visiting Edgar Street in Hereford. It’s a proper old school stadium with loads of history. I love the Meadow End behind the goal (maybe I’m even a little jealous!

). The home fans create a great atmosphere too. To be honest, even if I didn’t like the trip, I’d probably still choose Hereford just for a burger from The Beefy Boys.

If you know, you know! Who was your club’s Player of the Season? It’s got to be captain Will Thornton.

He cleaned up! Winning the management, supporters' and players' player of the season awards. He was outstanding throughout the campaign, leading the side through what was arguably the toughest season in the club’s history.

Despite being tipped by many for relegation, he captained the club to their first ever National League North play-off appearance. A proper leader on and off the pitch, and fully deserving of every award he received. What was the single best moment of last season?

For me it was the late winner away at Darlington in April, scored by none other than captain Will Thornton! It secured three vital points in our push for the play-offs and honestly when that goal went in, I felt for certain we’d get there. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Paul Blackett from South Shields. I’d sign anyone who’s bringing 30 goals a season. Nobody can argue the importance of goals.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? What advice can I give a Manchester United treble winner? Absolutely none.

I’d probably spend the two minutes trying to find out who’s signing next and pretending it wasn’t me who asked. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? I’d love a bigger terrace behind the goal.

Like the Meadow End at Edgar Street! There's just something about a big terrace behind a goal, it gets the atmosphere going. You can’t beat it.

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? I think Morecambe will bounce straight back. They’ve appointed a top manager in Adam Lakeland and he has already made some great signings.

Of course, I’ll probably be wrong! Who’ll be the surprise package? Scarborough Athletic again of course!

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We played away from home for ten years before returning to Scarborough in 2017.

article.title: The Fans' View: South Shields aim to alleviate a triple bout of agony
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Edged out in the title race on the final day of season when they had sat top of so long, and second best in an agonising Promotion Final. Then, weeks later, head coach Ian Watson departs to take up the vacant managerial position at Rochdale. Doom and gloom this summer at South Shields, then?

Far from it. They’ve kept the majority of their team together and with Mike Williamson taking over, confidence is high that the club can go one better and secure that historic promotion. Williamson says he has nothing to prove to anyone as he returns to the North East where his managerial career really took off at Gateshead.

Shields fan Joe Woods thinks the bitter ending to last season will only spur his club on in their quest as he looks ahead to 2026/27. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Slowly coming together. Fixture release day is on Friday - who’s your ideal first day opponent?

I would ideally like to be at home but I don’t really mind who we play. It could be an advantage playing a potential promotion rival like Morecambe or Chester who have made lots of changes to their team which could take time for them to fully integrate. What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season?

I’m most looking forward for Morecambe. The ground looks excellent and the town looks like a great place for a weekend trip, so I would hope for the fixture to be on a Saturday towards the end of the season. I’m also looking forward for the derby against Hebburn which is only two stops away on the metro from our ground.

What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in Paul Blackett without a doubt. I think he would be very hard to replace with the amount of goals he scores for us. With one year left on his contract I would hope that he remains a Shields player for the upcoming season.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? My advice for Mike Williamson would be to continue to build off the foundation that Ian Watson built last season. In terms of signings this summer, I would recommend him to look at players who can provide some physicality to our squad as there were times last season where our lack of physicality was an issue especially away from home.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? I think there needs to be a solution for when it comes to away fans. If we ever get promoted to the National League, we will most likely have to give away teams a larger allocation than we do now.

In the Promotion Final, we gave Kidderminster 1,200 tickets, which meant giving them the section where the Sima Shed is and moving the fans who usually stand in the Sima Shed to the other side of the stadium, which has a lot less room than the normal side and it was congested. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Anything can happen , especially in this league, but Morecambe look the strongest team right now.

Adam Lakeland is a great manager and they have had an impressive transfer window so far. But you can’t write off the likes of Brackley, Macclesfield, Chester and of course South Shields. Who’ll be the surprise package?

I personally think Hednesford will be the surprise package this season. After winning the play-off in the Northern Premier League last season, I can see them pushing for a top seven place in the National League North this season. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Christian Dibble from Macclesfield. I seen him play against South Shields a few times last season including in the Promotion Final where he pulled off some great saves for Kidderminster and was a major part of their success in the play-offs last season. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

Between 2013 and 2015, the club had to leave Mariners Park and relocated 20 miles down the road in Peterlee due to struggles off the pitch. Fortunately, our time at Peterlee was only short and we were able to move back home after Geoff Thompson bought both the club and Mariners Park.

article.title: The Fans' View: Southport look to set the standard with a week to go
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
In exactly one weeks’ time, the new season will be here - and August gives all fans those few days to dream big. Southport’s supporters are no different and they are wondering if more steps forward can be taken. It will take a lot to top the club’s FA Trophy run, bowing out at the semi-final stage to eventual winners Southend United.

There’s perhaps room for improvement in the Enterprise National League North, but as Neil Danns plots his second season at the helm, confidence is growing that the team could be a fixture in the top half of the table this time around. The countdown is on, and Sandergrounder Liam Doyle takes us inside his club with the 2026/27 campaign edging ever closer. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Glass half full.

What are your expectations for next season - and can they be achieved I think most fans would have taken 60 points, a great FA Trophy run and not too many worries over relegation last season. Every season should be about improving on the last. What ground are you looking forward to visiting?

We’ve got two corkers in August, Hebburn Town followed two weeks later by Hednesford. I’m a groundhopper so two new ticks hopefully. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in It has to be super Danny Lloyd.

It’s always a pleasure watching him play. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? I wouldn’t give him advice, but I would simply tell Neil Danns that so far so good.

There were always going to be tough moments in his first year but for me the signs and encouraging. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Absolutely nothing.

Haig Avenue is famously one of the best Non-League grounds in the country. The only change I would make is the level of football played on it! It would be great to go up after years away.

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? This won’t go down well but I’m going to say Chester. This might be more about piling the pressure on!

Who’ll be the surprise package? Oxford City will be a lot better this time around and will make the play-offs. A few of the new clubs will do well, I like what Spalding United and Hednesford are doing.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Paul Blackett at South Shields would get into any team in the division and the one above. We probably couldn’t afford his left foot mind you.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? The club actually begun as a rugby team back in the 1870s. As soon as a new manager comes in who likes to go long, the predictable jokes are made.

article.title: Welcome to the Enterprise National League North: Spalding United
article.author: Tom Scott
article.html:
Here is the lowdown on Enterprise National League North Spalding United ahead of the new season. Factfile Last Season: Southern League Premier Central – Play-Off Final winners Top Scorer: Jack Roberts (28) Manager: Jimmy Dean Ground: Sir Halley Stewart Field Best National League Performance: N/A How they got here... Spalding United were established in 1905 through the merger of Fulney Institute and Victoria, and have spent over a century navigating the Lincolnshire and Midlands non-league landscape.

The club has known adversity: a near-liquidation in the early 1990s interrupted a steady if circuitous rise. But after losing the 2022-23 Division One Midlands play-off final 2-1 to Halesowen Town, the following season they won the division outright. Their second campaign at Step 3 in 2025-26 produced 25 wins, 10 draws, and a remarkable 103 league goals, topped off by a play-off run that ended in the kind of drama the format was made for.

They beat Halesowen in the semi-final – sweet revenge for 2023 – and then faced Real Bedford in the final. 2,700 supporters squeezed into Sir Halley Stewart Field to witness the late drama – they needed a 92nd-minute penalty to force extra time, where they ultimately won 4-2. Next season marks the club’s first appearance in the National League setup – though they’ve already had the beating of a couple of Step 2 clubs, as both Alfreton and Dagenham & Redbridge exited the FA Cup to the Tulips this season.

Keep an eye out for... Frontman Jack Roberts was an integral part in the Tulips’ promotion last season – so much so they’ve tied him down to a three-year deal ahead of their first National League North campaign. Last season he notched 28 goals and registered 22 assists.

Say no more. Main Image: Keira Thurston/Adrian Smith

article.title: The Fans' View: Moor promotions would make Spennymoor merrier!
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
When you’ve been on upward trajectory for the first half of your existence, sometimes playing the waiting game can become a little frustrating. It felt like non-stop promotions and cup finals for Spennymoor Town when the club was born in 2005. But since they joined the National League North in 2017, they’ve not been able to take a big next step and grab another.

On what will be the tenth anniversary of their Northern League success, supporters are wondering if they things are about to perfectly align. In our latest fan season preview, Simon Gardener sees no reason why Spennymoor can’t re-start the party. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Getting excited now.

What are your expectations for next season - and can they be achieved. After missing out by five points last season, I think we have to be looking at a play-off run again. That’s the hope but it’s getting harder every year.

What ground are you looking forward to visiting? Hebburn Town. Our clubs are about half an hour away but I don’t think we’ve ever played in a league or cup match.

It is a way off but I’m sure we’ll take great numbers on Good Friday. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in The man and the legend Glen Taylor. He’s scored over 200 goals for the club and at 36 I would be gutted if he didn’t finish his career here.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Tommy Miller showed that fans enough in the final few months of last season to earn the job, and earn a little patience. My advice, or request, would be to only keep improving.

Let’s get as many young local lads involved as possible. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Nothing.

Not now the pitch has seen real investment this summer. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? I’m going to go with Morecambe, providing they start well.

If they don’t, South Shields will really fancy their chances this time despite losing their manager to Rochdale. Who’ll be the surprise package? I’m not sure you can be classed as ‘surprise’ if you’ve just signed Britt Assombalonga, but Harborough Town could do well.

I also expect Hereford to be a lot better, they had a hard season. The same goes for Chorley. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Matty Stenson [AFC Telford] has always impressed me. I would have loved us to sign Tyrone Marsh this summer but he has gone to Oxford City. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

Spennymoor Town FC has only actually been around since 2005. The club was born out of the demise of both Spennymoor United AFC and Evenwood Town FC. Just a few years after its creation, Spennymoor Town won the FA Vase.

PHOTOS: DAVID NELSON

article.title: The Fans' View: Second season worries? Not at Worksop Town
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Beware second season syndrome. It’s the yearly reminder to clubs who have thrived at the first attempt, and are now looking for something even more . But if Worksop Town are worried, they’re really not showing it.

The Tigers navigated a tricky first Enterprise National League North season where the club were pretty much unbothered about a return to where they had come. An encouraging summer of recruitment and a solid pre-season has left supporters looking towards the big kick-off with relish - not worry. In the concluding week of our special fan features, Tony Dudley talks up his team’s chances and previews the runners and the riders ahead of the opening day.

Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words. Always looking forward. What are your expectations for next season — and are they achievable?

I haven’t been to many pre-season matches but from what I have read online there is competition for places in most positions and the squad is really shaping up. I think a top half finish is realistic. What ground are you looking forward to visiting?

I’m hoping to get to Chester in September. They’re a big club for this level and it wasn’t so long ago they were putting Wrexham in their place. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in We’ve lost a few of the fan favourites this summer.

Oli Greaves and Liam Waldock would both be big misses and hopefully they stay. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Craig Parry has done great things for this club.

He said this summer that we’ve lost players because teams below us are paying more money so I would just say stick to your guns. Playing for Worksop Town has to come before anything else. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

Plans for new terraces and extra turnstiles were given the go ahead earlier this year. We’re taking it step by step and not running before we can walk. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

It’s between South Shields and Morecambe if they can get off to a good start. Chester under Phil Parkinson shouldn’t be out of the conversation either. Who’ll be the surprise package?

Brackley Town. They’ve got a really good manager in Andy Whing and have signed really well. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Paul Blackett, the forward at South Shields. Even when he’s not having a great season he scored 20 league goals. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?
