There’s a big debate about when the club started. Some say it was in 1861, but others aren’t so sure and think the club formed in the 1870s. I looked online recently at an article on the subject, and one of the earliest games at the club was Married Gentlemen vs Unmarried Solicitors and Shopkeepers around 150 years ago!

article.title: The Fans' View: AFC Totton looking to throw another Stag party!
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
As first seasons go, there were few complaints from anyone at AFC Totton after an impressive debut campaign. A top half finish was just reward after taking to the Enterprise National League South like a duck to water. At one point, a play-off push looked on and not even the departure of manager Jimmy Ball to Torquay United could rock the boat.

Scott Rendell was as good a goalscorer as there was at Luton Town, Eastleigh, Woking and Aldershot. Now he takes the team, and wants to build on the foundations laid. We asked Dave Wood to talk us through the Stags’ first season at this level - and look ahead to the all important second.

Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Improvement, Consistent, Optimistic What are your expectations for next season — and are they achievable? Last season was our first ever at this level, so I think most fans had pretty low expectations - just avoiding the drop was enough to keep us happy. In the end, we finished comfortably mid-table.

So this year, I think a realistic expectation is to consolidate that with another mid-table finish. As much as the fans would love to see us pushing for a play-off spot, I think there are many other clubs with bigger budgets, bigger fan bases, and much better chances of reaching the play-offs. So personally, I think if we end up mid-table I would be happy.

What ground are you looking forward to visiting? I have to admit I don't get to too many away grounds at this level due to personal circumstances, but our nearest rivals Salisbury are not far away and it's always an entertaining match between the two clubs! There's a bit of history when our paths have crossed over the past few years, and both clubs are always desperate to win those matches, so the atmosphere is usually pretty good.

What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in That would have to be our very own "goal machine" Tony Lee. He's such a strong, powerful forward and has scored so many goals for Totton over the last few years. He's great in the air, and probably scores just as many with his head as his feet.

But he also gets back to help in defence and can often be found making crucial clearances in the box. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Advice?

I don't think Scott Rendell needs to hear any advice from me - he joined us as our striker having had a very successful career in both National League and EFL football. He became our manager towards the end of last season, and I think the relationship he has with our players will be key to his success this year. Maybe I'd just tell him to keep his boots handy and not rule out making a few more appearances on the pitch just yet - we just might need him!

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Well, funny you should say that - but the lack of a roof over the standing areas has been a contentious issue for our fans for a while. But this summer the club are installing a new covered standing stand at one end of the ground, which hopefully will be finished in time for the start of the season.

That combined with the promised new scoreboard and additional toilets should be a big improvement to the ground. I think we just need to keep improving and increasing capacity so that we can move forward and compete with the big boys in this league. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

Judging by some of the new signings over the summer I think there's a few clubs who will be favourites to win the league. Dagenham and Dorking are both strong contenders, but I think my prediction would be Torquay. Our previous manager Jimmy Ball left Totton towards the end of last season to join Torquay, and I wouldn't bet against him taking the club to the next level.

With the resources they have and the big fan base, combined with his shrewd recruitment and network of contacts, I think they stand a very good chance of winning the league. Who’ll be the surprise package? I'm hearing lots of good things about Farnham.

They're new to the league and people tend to underestimate the new boys (as we discovered last year!). But I think they will surprise a few people with how well they do this year.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? I think we still need another experienced and proven goalscorer in our squad. Someone like Torquay's Deon Moore would fit the bill.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Totton were one of the first clubs to play at the new Wembley Stadium, reaching the FA Vase Final in 2007 just as the stadium had reopened after being completely rebuilt. Unfortunately they lost to Truro City - who incidentally return to the National League South this season, so we will get a rematch with them!

article.title: Welcome to the Enterprise National League South: Billericay Town
article.author: Tom Scott
article.html:
Here is the lowdown on Enterprise National League South Billericay Town ahead of the new season. Factfile Last Season: Isthmian League – Play-Off Final Winners Top Scorer: Alfie Cerulli (14) Manager: Danny Scopes Ground: New Lodge Best National League Performance: 8th – National League South (2018-19) How they got here... Billericay Town have been here before – twice, in fact so it’s more a ‘Welcome back’ rather than just ‘Welcome’.

The Essex club had a single season in the Conference South in 2012-13 and returned again in 2017-18 by winning the Isthmian League Premier under the brief, chaotic, and headline-grabbing ownership of Glenn Tamplin, whose high-profile signings included Jamie O'Hara, Paul Konchesky and Jermaine Pennant. They were relegated after four seasons in 2021-22, finishing bottom. Before all that, they were already one of non-league's most decorated clubs – three FA Vase wins in four years between 1976 and 1979 remain a record that stands today.

The 2025-26 campaign, their third season back in the Isthmian Premier after relegation, started in rather unassuming fashion – but in the new year, they were a different beast. Two defeats and a draw in their final 20 games… they won the rest. The play-off final against Brentwood Town on 4 May brought 3,200 to New Lodge; the decisive goal came in the 117th minute of extra time to seal a 2-1 win.

They return to the National League South for the first time since 2022. Keep an eye out for... Charlie Ruff is a name many fans of National League South clubs will be familiar with.

After joining Billericay halfway through their campaign last season, he’ll be desperate to make a name for himself from the off this season. He’s always worth backing to produce something. Main image - Nicky Hayes

article.title: The Fans' View: Iron returning to a place which holds sweet memories
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
In the end, it wasn't the best of seasons for Braintree Town - but it’s not all bad news. There aren't many fans of National League clubs tuning into the World Cup to watch one of their players! While the Iron lick their wounds, defender Tommy Smith has been selected by New Zealand as they try to shut out Mo Salah and some other big names.

If history is anything to go by, the club’s relegation isn’t the end of the world. They are about to return to a league they’ve had great success in after winning promotion in 2011, 2018 and in 2024. We asked Scott Weaver to pick out some high points in a tough season as the Essex side look to the future.

Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? Not the best! What ground did you love visiting the most?

Carlisle is an absolute classic of a ground, I always find it bizarre that clubs like Braintree can play at these top top grounds, Who was your club’s Player of the Season? Mason Terry is the very obvious choice but I'd also like to throw Aidan Francis-Clarke into the mix too, What was the single best moment of last season? Aidan Francis-Clarke's last second winner against Truro City.

It was an absolute must win game and we came from behind to win 3-2. I haven't screamed so hard in a while, and you can even hear it on the highlights! If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Alfie Matthews! The boy needs to come home, he was an absolute joy to watch and speak to in his last spell. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

I've spent a lot of time with Steve Pitt over the season so I think he's heard enough! What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? The facilities definitely need an update, the ground itself is more than suitable and a proper classic ground, we just need to strip out the basics It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

National League, I'd say Forest Green Rovers. National League South, where we're heading, I'm going with Dagenham & Redbridge. Who’ll be the surprise package?

Worthing won't be a pushover in the National League at all - they're a solid side with a good manager. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Braintree Town are only team in the country to have a floodlight on their badge!

article.title: The Fans' View: Cooper's plotting the Clarets' path to promotion
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
This time last year, Chelmsford City were one of a number of Enterprise National League South clubs causing a stir with the quality of their signings. Ultimately, none of them went up.They very much weren’t alone in this of course, but the Clarets couldn’t even make the play-offs.

Some 12 months have passed and again they’re being spoken about - but this time Mark Cooper and John Still are piloting the ship, and both very much know how to plot a path promotion. We’re asking a fan from every club to give us their experiences of last season while of course looking forward to the new one. Step forward City diehard Luke Iszatt , who knows what he wants to see when the campaign kicks off in under two months’ time.

Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? Hit and miss. What ground did you love visiting the most?

The ground I most enjoyed visiting in the league last season was Bath City, where we run out 1-0 victors. I really love the ‘old school’ feel to the ground and massive terraces around the stadium. Furthermore, the people at the club are very friendly and it was a shame to see them relegated!

Who was your club’s Player of the Season? Lyle Taylor. This due to the sheer amount of goals he scored which kept us in the hunt for the play-off positions right until the last couple games of the season.

I’d hate to think where Chelmsford may have finished without his goals! his leadership qualities and experience of playing in the EFL helped some of our younger players such as Harry Barbrook and Archie Tamplin have exceptional seasons. What was the single best moment of last season?

Young Jett Murphy’s 97th minute equaliser away at Dagenham to level the game at 3-3 after being 3-1 down and a man down. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Courtney Senior from Farnborough would be a strong choice for me.

An exciting winger who can add goals to any team. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? If I had any advice for Mark Cooper it would be that our amazing and growing fanbase are behind you and the team.

As long as we all see a team that is committed, dedicated and one that works hard that’s all we can ask for and hopefully our quality and experience will shine through and take us to promotion! What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? It’s probably extremely obvious and I’m sure everyone associated with the club would agree - get rid of the running track and move the stands closer to the pitch!

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? It’s an extremely tight, competitive and unpredictable division however I have to back my team Chelmsford to go all the way and win it! Who’ll be the surprise package?

That would be Folkestone Invicta. Coming off the back of comfortably winning the Isthmian Premier last season by a 12 point margin, I believe they can carry on the momentum and have a good season after going up. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

That we are the longest serving club in the division having completed 18 seasons at the level without promotion or relegation in that period.

article.title: The Fans' View: 'Keeping underestimating my Chesham United at your peril!"
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Things are challenging enough for Chesham United with the Enterprise National League South in double figures for full-time clubs. Not only do most of the sides they come up against have more resources, but the Generals face another battle - they have to play the first three games of the season away from home. The Meadow is undergoing a massive reconstruction to fix severe drainage issues and level the playing field and the club are going to reap the benefits.

James Duncan and Michael Murray have certainly set a high bar for progress after the team’s excellent 11th-place finish last season. Chesham fan Alex Barker is looking forward to seeing his team take to the field on their new surface at the end of August and hopes they can keep disrupting the big boys! Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Getting Pitch Ready.

We’ve spent £200.000 getting it done. Which hopefully means we won’t keep getting games called off over the winter months as last season, we were having them go on a regular basis.

What are your expectations for next season - and can they be achieved? Realistically? Mid-table but hopefully challenge for the play-offs.

For the size of the club and the budget we have, we shouldn’t be anywhere near the top seven. We surprise a lot of the league’s so-called big boys. What ground are you most looking forward to visiting?

Hampton & Richmond Borough. Was meant to take my daughter to her first Chesham away game last season and it was called off the morning of the game due to a frozen pitch. We went shopping in central London instead.

What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in Alex Lafleur. He could easily play in the national league but he is head of sports in a top school in the local area and remains loyal to Chesham. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s managers - what advice would you give him?

No advice. James Duncan and Michael Murray just get this club and the area. Watch, Chesham All In and you will understand.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? The pitch definitely, but that’s about to change with the pitch being relaid. Nothing else.

It’s a proper Non-League ground. Maybe more toilets! It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

Well, If. Dagenham don’t win it, they should be embarrassed with the players they are signing. But just ask Dorking.

It doesn’t work out that way. Who’ll be the surprise package? Chesham!

Tiny budget for this level and small crowds maybe, but we but always surprise the so called bigger teams. Ask Marc White and Dorking, who we took four points off last season. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

I would like to take Josh Addae back from Dagenham who has just left us for them, this summer. They have a player there. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know?

The Tea Bar. Well worth a visit!

article.title: The Fans' View: The Daggers need to be sharper this time
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
There’s hardly a club more talked about outside the EFL than Dagenham & Redbridge. A former England striker up top and a superstar streamer on the board is always likely to keep you front and centre. But year one of the project hardly sent out a message to the rest - and now the pressure is on for the east London club to come up with some answers after failing the threaten the promotion places.

But so far the club not only have a new manager to bed in, but 13 new players too. Jeff from the Dag & Red podcast knows it won’t be easy this time either and after the fixtures were released on Friday, he talks us through the ten months ahead. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Hopeful, cautiously optimistic What are the expectations at Dagenham & Redbridge next season - and what can be achieved?

After finishing a disappointing 13th last season and never really being in with a chance of play-offs, the expectation is a bare minimum of the top seven this time round. With new owners, a new manager and virtually a new team, we are full of optimism. But realistically fans know there are other teams who probably feel the same.

So play-offs at least is the aim with a hint of hope for better. What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season? There's a few new grounds that I have never been too and it’s always good to see new stadiums.

As Cornwall is one of my favourite destinations, I think a trip to Truro City is top of the list. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in As we have signed 13 new players to date and in Joe Haigh already lost a player I'd really want to keep that is hard to say. But Andy Carroll if he can stay fit will get goals and cause havoc at this level.

So as I'm sure a lot of our planning will be around him. I'd hate to see him go but as he is a joint owner and assistant manager, I think he'll stay! You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

I dont think it would be news to Lee Allinson if I told him we want to see commitment team with a never-say-die attitude. The last few years the feeling has been we haven't quite had that. The manager seems to have recognised that about us in his interviews.

The second thing would be to tell him not to come out after a game and tell us we were good when we weren't. He seems a straight talker to me, I think that will go down well. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

Unusually for almost any level away fans with a big following can get the best seats in the ground which dilutes the home advantage. I can see financially the need, but in a perfect world this would change. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

I expect it to be as competitive as it ever has been if not even more so. The usual suspects Dorking, Chelmsford, Torquay and Weston-super-Mare will be up there and hopefully Daggers will be too. Its probably too early to say but if I had to choose I'll say the experience Chelmsford have added may make them favourites Who’ll be the surprise package?

There are a few clubs more than capable of gatecrashing the party. Maidenhead, Maidstone United, Truro City, Ebbsfleet or Hemel - but someone who might take a leap from last seasons 19th place is Farnborough. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Lyle Taylor of Chelmsford looked quality against us last season and scored about 20 goals so as goals are always a vital quality I'll go for him What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? You might find yourself in the best seat in the house and bar one or two idiots, and all clubs have them, you'll have a good welcome and experience.

article.title: The Fans' View: 'I was part of Dorking's matchday squad, nothing can beat that!'
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
His team might have fallen just short in their quest for promotion, but Terry Dunn had an experience not many supporters ever have. Following an injury to Dorking Wanderers goalkeeper Harrison Foulkes, the 54-year-old former local goalkeeper got a call from Marc White asking him to relieve the pressure. After signing the forms and training, he made the matchday squad and although he didn’t get on in their Enterprise National League South fixture against AFC Totton he had an experience he will never forget.

Terry has been on duty again - but shot saving isn’t required. This time the Dorking fan has been taking part in our end of season review, and it’s no surprise to discover what his favourite moment was! Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season?

Too. Many. Injuries.

What ground did you love visiting the most? I really enjoyed our trip to Dagenham & Redbridge. We took big support down there and had a good day, even if it wasn’t the result we wanted.

Who was your club’s Player of the Season? Luke Moore. Always gave his best even if he never made the squad.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? We’ve already got him! Isacc Philpot.

He’s an old-school defender who should really help the team next season. What was the single best moment of last season? Not many fans will give you this answer!

Being part of squad for a day. When I was part of the match day squad when the gaffer put a shout out after an injury to our goalkeeper Harrison Foulkes. He signed me up and told the press I was 60!

He asked me to go to the club and have a photo taken, the next thing I know I’m all over social media! I didn’t play in the end but I had a penalty shoot-out with the kids and got a real insight to what goes on. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

Just keep doing what you’re doing. It has worked well enough for the last 26 years! Marc White is Mr Dorking and if it wasn’t for him, there would be no club.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Cover down the side to keep people dry. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

I have to say Dorking Wanderers! I think we could win the league because we have signed a few players in certain areas we needed already. Also, we’re trying to short out physio department, which was an issue last year with injuries costing us dear.

Who’ll be the surprise package? Chesham United. They were a good side last year, just missed out and after a few years in the league they’ve now found their feet.

The Generals are a club looking for promotion. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We never boo the players off, even if the result has gone pear shaped.

article.title: The Fans' View: Dover don't want to be looking down this time
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Some supporters needed the close-season to arrive more than others. Dover Athletic die-hards had just about enough of 2025/26 by the time the end of April rolled around, even if it was mission accomplished at Crabble. Eight losses in their last 11 National League South matches and just five wins in 2026 saw the club crawl over the line, as a once encouraging season saw the Whites end the campaign one place above the drop zone.

Jake Leberl said there is no room for sentiment this summer as changes were made. We’re speaking to a fan from every club as we look ahead to 2026/27, and Steve Arnold gives us the inside track as Dover look for a do-over. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Big improvement needed.

What are your expectations for next season - and can they be achieved. Well if we start this season how we ended the last it will be a battle against relegation. The standard of the league will be a lot better at that end, make no mistake.

A stable mid-table season should be the exception but it won’t be easy. What ground are you looking forward to visiting? Billericay Town on the first day of the season.

Not too far from home and there should be a good crowd. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in Roman Charles-Cook. He’s just signed a new contract, so not much chance he’ll be leaving.

He’s been here for four or five years now, so pleased with that. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Jake Leberl has the backing of most of the fans, and I would tell him that.

But we need a solid start after the last few months of last season. I’d advise him to get more money from the chairman! What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

Crabble is a brilliant Non-League ground, I just want more people inside it. Some more entry deals would be a good start. We’re not the most expensive, but some extra marketing is needed here and there for sure.

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? It’s surely got to be Torquay United’s turn? They’ve been here a while.

A season too soon for Dagenham I think but Dorking have signed well, including one of ours! Who’ll be the surprise package? Braintree Town.

They specialise in this level of football. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? George Nikaj from Dorking.

They took him off us in May and I’m still not over it. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We have been under the same ownership for more than two decades.

Jim Parmenter saved the club when it was on the brink of extinction back in 2005 and he is still in control now.

article.title: The Fans' View: A case of so nearly for recovering Ebbsfleet
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
It’s safe to say Ebbsfleet United fans didn’t quite know what to expect heading into 2025/26. They had watched their side be relegated by mid-March after finishing an eye-watering 31 points from safety, and everyone had the same question - just how do you get a team winning most weeks after just three in ten months? Things could only get better and Josh Wright so nearly came up with the perfect answer, with only goal difference keeping the Kent club from a play-off finish.

Ebbsfleet posted an impressive 55 point improvement from the horror season before and in a league littered with full-time clubs, they at least showed their powers of recovery. Fan and journalist Joshua Peck talks us through the season and picks his surprise package who could create havoc in the push for promotion. Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season?

Should’ve been better. What ground did you love visiting the most Salisbury’s. Not so much for the game - we conceded another stoppage time equaliser.

This game was Fleet fans’ designated away weekender. A great weekend, bar the last five minutes of the football. Who was your club’s Player of the Season?

Ben Chapman got the official pick, and it’s hard to look past him. Nine goals and six assists for Mr Reliable. Jake Hessenthaler deserves a mention too.

In his first year with the club, the veteran midfielder impressed, keeping a calm head in the middle of the pitch and popping up with a few crucial goals, too. Charlie Seaman was solid at right-back as well. What was the single best moment of last season?

Opening day at Dagenham. The hosts were among the favourites to go up and we won 2-0. The sun was shining and we played well.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Worthing’s Razzaq Coleman De-Graft tore us apart on the last day of the season. Pace and wanting to drive forward… that’d be nice.

Fired home from 20 yards to seal promotion for Worthing on that final day to show he’s more than speed and skill. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Please stop dropping so deep when leading late on.

We conceded so many late equalisers, including four stoppage time equalisers in five games at one point. Keep hold of one of those wins and we are comfortably in the play-offs. Attack is the best form of defence, so keep going forward.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? More terracing, please. Since the new main stand was built at Stonebridge Road, there are very few places to stand and watch the game.

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Hard to look past Torquay. They had a strong end to the season, agonisingly losing the play-off final, and Jimmy Ball looks like a great fit in the south west.

Who’ll be the surprise package? Folkestone Invicta. They romped to the Isthmian Premier title and will cause a few upsets a level higher.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Striker Kwesi Appiah previously played in an AFCON final for Ghana.

article.title: The Fans' View: Boro's late burst and great goals live long in the memory!
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Farnborough fans were given a warning before the season started by their realistic manager Spencer Day. He told them the Enterprise National League South is more demanding that it has ever been before, and while accurate prophecy had become hard the division was now a machine like he’d never witnessed before. Day probably wouldn’t have admitted it at the time, but he may well have taken finishing ten points above the drop zone.

The club’s topsy-turvy season was perhaps best illustrated by their final two games - a 6-1 home defeat to Tonbridge Angels, and a 6-1 win at AFC Totton. We asked Boro supporter Thomas Ryan to review their campaign, predict what could be ahead and name the ground he loved going to. Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season?

Busy. Exhilarating . Fun.

What ground did you love visiting the most Every time I have visited Salisbury’s Raymac I have been really captivated by the atmosphere it provides. It feels like a very fitting place to watch Enterprise National League South football. A proper away end, segregated, and directly facing the big stand of home fans really captures the essence of this level of football for me.

Who was your club’s Player of the Season? Hakeem Sandah was my player of the season by some distance. What he provided to the team felt like it couldn’t have been honoured by any statistical metric.

He managed to capture the imagination of the fans with his flair, and was the only player who could always give us something to cheer for. I believe without his contributions, we’d have been relegated. What was the single best moment of last season?

Louie Holzman's late winner against Chippenham. Not only at the time was such a brilliant moment to celebrate, but also the implications of that goal would be season-saving for the club. A close second would be going 2-0 up within the first ten minutes at Dorking away, with two incredible goals from Amir Hadi and Renny Smith.

The latter was later named Goal of the Season. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? AFC Totton’s AFC Bournemouth loanee Ashley Clarke is a standout player who I think flew under the radar.

I think he would add not only tenacity to our side, but also largely contribute goals and assists in the attacking department. I view him as multi-faceted force which can only aid any side who wants to play attacking football. Additionally, Reggie Young is a player that any Farnborough fan would love to see back in yellow and blue for many of the same reasons.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager. What advice would you give him? I would say to Spencer Day that consistency is key and that he should do anything to keep our core group of players all season long, albeit easier said than done for the club.

The mid-season “revolving door” has hurt us many times before. I would also say that I don’t think we should ever push away from playing a forward thinking brand of football. As a fanbase, we have been treated to some really exiting players, who have consistently captured the imagination with attacking football.

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Cherrywood Road is something us Farnborough fans can really boast about. It’s a large, but simultaneously soulful ground that has really epitomises “home”.

If I had to make one change, I would like to see us possibly use just a bit more yellow colouring around the ground. It’s possibly one of the only things we could add to make it more “Boro”. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

Both Dorking’s and Dagenham’s business has really impressed me, but i’ll edge it to Dorking, thanks to more consistency within their squad. Who’ll be the surprise package? In terms of promoted sides, Farnham seem to be the obvious choice.

But I think Folkestone are being overlooked. Kevin Lokko is a defender who I think could still play way beyond the National League South, and I think he will keep them watertight at the back in their maiden season at this level. What’s one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don’t know?

Before Macclesfield took on and beat Palace this season, Farnborough Town were the last Non-League club to score against the reigning FA Cup winners in the competition. We scored a late consolation goal past the likes of Sol Campbell, Patrick Vieira and Robert Pires at Arsenal.

article.title: Welcome to the Enterprise National League South: Farnham Town
article.author: Tom Scott
article.html:
Here is the lowdown on Enterprise National League South Farnham Town ahead of the new season. Factfile Last Season: Southern League Premier South – Play-Off Final winners Top Scorer: Owen Dean (23) Manager: Paul Johnson Ground: The Memorial Ground Best National League Performance: N/A How they got here... Farnham Town were established in 1906 as a merger of Farnham Bungs and Farnham Star, and have spent most of their 119-year existence in the lower reaches of the Surrey and Combined Counties pyramid.

Ground grading issues at their Memorial Ground home has blocked promotion on more than one occasion across the decades – they won the Combined Counties League in 1990-91 and retained it the following season but resigned from the Isthmian League Division Three before the 1992-93 season began because they could not raise the money needed to upgrade the Memorial Ground. The recent trajectory has been very different. The 2023-24 season saw Farnham Town win their first 25 league matches – a national record – earning promotion to Step 4.

They followed up with a 102-point haul and the Isthmian League South Central title the following season, and continued their remarkable rise this season in the Southern League Premier Division South. Their play-off final against Gloucester City brought 2,200 to the Memorial Ground and a 5-1 win, thanks in part to a Billy Clifford hat-trick. Three straight promotions has earned a first appearance at Step 2, and in the National League setup, in the club's history.

Keep an eye out for... The list is endless but the signing of Rakish Bingham from Farnborough has shown Farnham Town are not coming into the National League South to make up the numbers. The former Ebbsfleet United man brings experience of the division and goals – he got 15 last term for the Boro.

Main Image: Farnham Town

article.title: Welcome to the Enterprise National League South: Folkestone Invicta
article.author: Tom Scott and Richard Dorman
article.html:
Here is the lowdown on Enterprise National League South Folkestone Invicta ahead of the new season. Factfile Last Season: Isthmian Premier League - Champions Top Scorer: Jake Hutchinson (24) Manager: Jay Saunders Ground: Alcaline Stadium Best National League Performance: N/A How they got here... Folkestone Invicta have never competed in the National League setup, though they did spend three seasons at the equivalent level – the Southern League Premier Division – between 2000 and 2003 under Neil Cugley, who went on to manage the club for a remarkable 26 seasons and over 1,300 matches before stepping down in 2022.

Founded in 1936, Invicta spent decades in local Kent football before acquiring the Cheriton Road ground in 1991 after the town's previous senior club folded and have called it home ever since – though not without interruption. The opening weeks of 2025-26 were spent playing home fixtures at Margate, Ashford and Chatham while a new 3G pitch was installed, and it was mid-October before Invicta returned to their own ground. Once settled, they were devastating.

A 12-game winning streak sent them clear at the top of the Isthmian Premier, and they were never seriously threatened. In the FA Cup, they beat National League South side Maidstone United 2-0 – a particularly charged tie given former Maidstone connections in the squad – before bowing out at promotion-chasing Southend. Jake Hutchinson and captain Kevin Lokko scored the goals that clinched the title 2-1 at St Albans on Easter Saturday, and nearly 2,600 packed Cheriton Road two days later for the trophy presentation.

Their arrival in the National League South promises to set the Kent non-league scene alight – Dover, Maidstone, Tonbridge and Ebbsfleet all currently inhabit the division, meaning a cluster of fierce local rivalries awaits. Keep an eye out for... Kevin Lokko has been an integral part of the side the romped to the Isthmian League title last season.

The 30-year-old defender notched the crucial goal in the game that confirmed Folkestone Invicta as champions. Stay tuned for more! Main Image - SharnVisuals

article.title: The Fans' View: Change coming at Hampton, but so much remains the same
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Things are changing at Hampton & RB this summer - but Alan Dowson remains very much part of the furniture. Returning to keep the club in the Enterprise National League South back in December after seven years away, the legendary Geordie transformed their fortunes. Now the club are transforming the Beveree.

A new synthetic pitch is going down in the weeks ahead, a decision described as vital to Hampton’s future. Last season the team took down some big hitters, showing what they’re capable of. The manager has the summer he wanted to get his squad battle-ready for what he says is the toughest division he has known.

We asked young supporter Tommy Rance for some of his highlights - and has a wish-list for his manager! Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? Challenging, inconsistent, relief.

What ground did you love visiting the most I enjoyed visiting a couple of new grounds in Horsham and AFC Totton, but the best for me is Salisbury. I found it a proper ground with big stands on both sides, and a smaller stepped terrace behind the other goal. It had real character, and what a fantastic city to visit.

Who was your club’s Player of the Season? Reece Grego-Cox, the man that came up with moment after moment across the season, he was very important in turning our fortunes around. He's a very clever footballer and I'm thrilled to see him signed on for next season.

What was the single best moment of last season? Beating Dorking Wanderers 3-0 in their own backyard was really special, a very enjoyable afternoon with a superb upset to boot. Also ensuring safety at home to Chippenham was a fantastic day, and a proud day later in the season.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Sam Corne. Where to start - a fantastic footballer, intelligent and experienced.

Is easily one of the best players in the league, and gutted that Tonbridge have him signed, because a successful Maidstone side always looked brilliant with him in it. If not Hakeem Sandah at Farnborough last year, deservedly snapped up by Aldershot Town in the National League. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

Big fan of Dowse, has got everyone back truly pulling together in the same direction, and we all are right behind him. I'd advise him to bring a translator for his interviews jokingly, but to keep the exciting football - keep the honesty, which is a rare quality in managers of today, and use all of his experience to drag us up the table kicking and screaming. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

With the new synthetic pitch going down this summer, it is a time for change, but a lot of what’s happening is cause for excitement. I'd like to see a cover behind the goal closest to the bar, but I want us to keep the charm of the ground alive. Tonbridge put down a 3G pitch, and Longmead has still got an awful lot of character and I want us too as well.

It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Hampton, obviously! Oh OK then, if I must pick someone else then probably Dagenham, loads of time for Lee Allinson as a manager, superb appointment which I'm sure will lead them to success.

Who’ll be the surprise package? Billericay Town. Danny Scopes knows what he's doing, I wouldn't be surprised if he replicated his first season in the National League South with Aveley and led them to the upper echelons of the table.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We previously held a record for the most penalties taken in a shoot-out with 42 in a Middlesex Charity Cup fixture with Cockfosters! We lost 18-17 after a staggering 21 penalties each!

article.title: The Fans' View: It's back to the future for Hemel Hempstead
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Hemel Hempstead Town fans are dreaming - and not only about the World Cup. Their club is inching nearer to achieving its ultimate goal and the feeling at Vauxhall Road is that they are closer than they’ve ever been. They aren’t letting the fact their manager has been grabbed by another club gunning for promotion put them off.

Lee Allinson is out and Lee Bircham is back in, but the Tudors, who finished fifth last season, must contend with the loss of some of the players who took them to their highest height so far. Every day this summer we’re opening up the stage to a supporter to tell us more about their club. Here, Louie Doran tells us why fixture release day on Friday can’t come soon enough.

Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words. Exciting, Bright, Ambitious Fixture release day is on Friday. Who is your ideal first opponent and why?

Dagenham would be an interesting one, wouldn’t it! Definitely the one I am looking forward to, since our manager and a few players have left for them. It would be amazing when we beat them, and if we get to do it on opening day, even better!

What ground are you most looking forward to visiting next season and why? For me, all the newly promoted sides I am very excited to visit, as it will be my first time. Especially Farnham..

I love the old-fashioned feel to it! A great club on the up too, very excited for that away day. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a record-breaking fee came in?

Darion Dowrich, easily. We managed to keep hold of him for the upcoming season somehow. No doubt EFL clubs will be all over next summer, though.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager. What advice would you give him? Tough question!

I love everything Lee Bircham is doing currently. I would just tell him to enjoy it. Passion is so important for us fans.

If you love the club like we do, then we love you. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? Tough one again, as I love our ground.

I know the right answer here, though. I would definitely expand our car park, as parking around our ground is an absolute nightmare, especially when the big boys visit. It’s early days, but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

Wow, you have got me here. I usually wait until after pre-season to make any sort of predictions. Hemel, because what is the point of supporting if you do not believe!

Is that a sell-out answer? If it is, let’s say Dorking! Who’ll be the surprise package?

Glad you have asked this, as I get to speak about a team I have said countless times will be right up there next season! Farnham Town, easily. What a squad they are building.

No messing about from them. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Every question seems to get tougher and tougher!

I am going to go a little rogue and say Jayden Bennett from Chesham. Every time I watch him play, he is nothing short of magnificent. He needs to get a big move next summer!

What’s one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don’t know? Our badge features King Henry VIII, not just because we’re called the Tudors, but because he granted Hemel Hempstead its Royal Charter in 1539, giving the town a unique link to Tudor history.

article.title: The Fans' View: Horsham are hoping for another stable season
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
After promotion came stability, so what’s around the corner next for Horsham? There was nothing to be scared of after stepping into the Enterprise National League South last summer. The Hornets first ever season at this level was less daunting than maybe some predicted.

No flirtation with the bottom four, no drubbings and a 16-point cushion suggests they’re just getting started. In our latest fan review, supporter James Gould answers some key questions - who would he love to see in his club’s colours, who is it tipping for the title and why the fans are called the Lardy Army! Here’s what he had to tell us…..

Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Things look promising. Fixture release day is on Friday July 10 - who’s your ideal first day opponent? Anyone at home!

We lost every one of our last seven away matches last season. What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season? Folkestone Invicta.

We had some battles with them in our Ryman League days and it’s good to see them come up. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in My choice is Reece Myles-Meekums. He missed the final month of the season and it showed.

He could clock up 200 appearances for the club by the end of the season if he stays injury free. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Just keep the team improving every year.

Promotion the year before last was beyond what most of the fans expected, and so was staying up with ease last season. We’ve come very far in a short space of time. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

After years and years of trying to secure our future, there’s not much to complain about. Some extra supporter parking would maybe attract more casual fans. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

I’m interested to see what Mark Cooper does at Chelmsford City. I also think Torquay United, Dorking and Dagenham will be right up there and so will a team most people aren’t tipping, Truro City. Who’ll be the surprise package?

Farnborough have signed really well. They won’t struggle this time. Braintree Town know the level and will fly under the radar.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Sonny Lo-Everton was fantastic against Horsham for Torquay United. I would have said Charlie Carter but he is already a Sutton United player.

Great signing. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Many know the Lardy Army are the voice of the club but most don't know how they got their name.

The group has been going since the 1990’s when the fans thought it would be a good idea to leave a bar of lard at opposition clubs as a kind of ‘calling card’. One chairman complained because he was a little on the porky side and that’s how it all started.

article.title: The Fans' View: Magpies of Maidenhead taking flight.. even without Dev
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
After 913 matches in charge, this was the season Maidenhead United and Alan Devonshire decided on a parting of the ways. The former England international left after ten years in the York Road dug-out, and his number two Ryan Peters was charged with trying to salvage something from their season. After 31 straight years in management it was time for Dev to have a rest - and his replacement did a stand-up job, guiding the club into the play-offs.

Promotion came perhaps too soon after Eliminator defeat at Dorking Wanderers, but the legendary manager’s number two have provided hope for the future. We asked young fan Alfie Butler for his assessment - and for what he is looking forward to when football returns in August. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words.

Point to prove. Fixture release day is on Friday July 10 - who’s your ideal first day opponent? Dover away.

We had a trip to Dover early last season and the vibes were incredible. It’s an historic Non-League ground and it has that charm and atmosphere about it. Definitely one of my favourites.

What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season? Torquay United’s Plainmoor - it’s been a ground I’ve wanted to attend for a while now, but simply haven’t had the opportunity to. An ex-EFL ground, one of the biggest the division has ever seen.

Visiting Torquay would allow me to meet up with some old mates of mine, tick off the ground and hopefully enjoy some time near the seaside! What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in. Matt Robinson.

Matt was incredible last season and got my vote as Maidenhead Player of the Season. He put himself on the line when it mattered most. He commanded the team throughout the season alongside Will De Havilland, and his performances speak for themselves.

It would be a real shame to see him go. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? My advice would simply be to just keep at it.

Forced in half-way through the season as interim manager when Alan Devonshire’s long tenure ended, and he was left to connect the dots. Ending the season with two of a possible five Manager of the Month awards, first in points and wins since joining as interim manager. I don’t really think I could give advice.

Incredible job Peyo! What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? I would change the elevation of the Canal End stand, the viewing experience isn’t always the greatest.

So by adding more elevation and steps I think that issue could be resolved. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Maid….

Torquay. As much as I’d love Maidenhead to win the league I don’t think it will happen. Torquay have been bound for promotion for years now, and I believe this will be their year.

Who’ll be the surprise package? Folkestone, to win Step 3 last year with a points difference of 12 points is phenomenal. They’re my dark horse for the 2026/27 season.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? I would love to see Jordan Young in black and white. He’s the perfect replacement for Josh Popoola and we’ve been missing a left footed right winger for a while now.

He’s positive with the ball, loves to cut in onto his left foot and brushes passed defenders like they’re not even there. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Maidenhead United were apart of the inaugural FA Cup Competition in 1871/72.

Also only having missed only the 1876/77 FA Cup competition up to the present day.

article.title: The Fans' View: Fagan can step up and get the Stones rolling again
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Naturally, not all assistants go on to make great managers, but Craig Fagan is certainly going to have great fun trying - and hopes Maidstone United fans will too. George Elokobi’s number two landed the top job in May, but it’s not just building on his legacy that he has in mind. Fans loved Elokobi, who of course gave them one of the finest moments - but for many, the team weren’t on the frontfoot enough for their liking.

Fagan is relishing the opportunity after being entrusted to take the club forward, and says he wants the team to be more exciting to watch. Stones’ long time fan Ruth Pettifer can’t wait to see what he produces and answered our ten summer questions with the countdown to kick-off really on. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words New.

Manager. Decent. What are your expectations for next season - and can they be achieved?

To make the play-offs and to have a decent run in both FA competitions. We’ll have to wait and see! What ground are you looking forward to visiting?

Chesham United. I don’t often get food at grounds, but their selection is really good. Very much enjoyed the cake last season and I’m hoping they are still selling the curry wraps.

What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in George Fowler. Mr dependable, been with the club for years and we need a leader for the young squad. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

Craig Fagan was George Elokobi’s assistant so I would say make sure the side is defensively strong, like it was under George, but try to be more attacking. And please have a real go at the FA Trophy. It is the club’s best opportunity to get to Wembley.

The FA Cup is also really important. I would probably rather have a third round tie away at a Premier League club than make the National League South play-offs. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

Our stadium is excellent for the level but to be complete, a stand on the riverside. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Dorking Wanderers Who’ll be the surprise package?

Folkestone Invicta If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Luke Coulson at Weston-super-Mare. Impresses me every time I see him.

He looks effortless as he controls the midfield and is the ultimate playmaker in the division . What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? There’s a small group of us who were at the one of the biggest FA Cup shocks of all time when Maidstone beat Ipswich at Portman Road who had watched the Stones play at pretty much every level of the Non-League pyramid.

This was right from the D&J Tyres youth league on a Sunday, the season after Maidstone went bust and were expelled from the Football League, through the Kent County Leagues and then all the way up to the National League.

article.title: The Fans' View: 'Why my super Salisbury will 'panda' to no-one!'
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Salisbury’s new owner Ali Alhamad now has his feet under the Ray Mac table as he looks to fulfill the club’s "huge potential". His first season at the helm after last summer’s takeover was one of progress, having avoided the drop by just one point the year before. It may not have been the flirtation with promotion fans may have dreamed on when the Kuwaiti businessman's company Proleague Ltd become the Enterprise National League South side's new owners In the latest fan review, Salisbury supporter Dominic Savage talks us through what he saw - and what he hopes is the start of something special.

But there are other things we need to know too - like the complex story about why his club actually have a panda mascot! Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season? Poor.

Progress Promising What ground did you love visiting the most? As a fan who has followed the Whites home and away for many seasons, there was only one new ground on the map for me this season, and that was The Camping World Community Stadium to give it its full title, the home of Horsham. It is an absolute gem of a place.

A lovely, welcoming community club driven by fantastic fans and a small army of dedicated volunteers who make you feel welcome the second you walk through the turnstiles. Who was your club’s Player of the Season? My choice is Josh Keeya.

He might be a bit of a left-field pick among the Salisbury faithful, but he is the ultimate unsung hero, the kind of player who does all the gruelling, unglamorous hard work that isn't always noticed by the casual observer. You know exactly what you are going to get from him every single week; his work rate and defensive discipline give the team its balance. What was the single best moment of last season?

In a challenging season, the absolute pinnacle had to be Dominic Revan’s stoppage-time winner at home against our Wiltshire - and relegation - rivals, Chippenham Town. It was a classic, cold, wet Tuesday night under the lights, but the atmosphere inside the Ray Mac was electric with over 1,700 fans packed in. In the dying moments of the match, a corner came swinging in from the right, Revan completely lost his marker, read the flight of the ball perfectly, and met it with a sublime side-footed volley straight into the back of the net.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Rather than taking the easy route and naming an out-and-out goalscorer like Louis Britton or Brad Dolaghan, I’m being realistic and looking at Sol Wanjau-Smith from Chippenham Town. He is the ultimate 'love to have him' in your team, hate to play against him' player.

He’s always possessed blistering pace, has an eye for goal, and is incredibly clever at drawing fouls in dangerous areas. But it’s not just what he does on the pitch that excites me. Sol has built a massive online presence, particularly on TikTok, where he has well over 100,000 followers.

You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? If I had two minutes with Brian Dutton, I’d just remind him of what got us here: the dressing room culture. The absolute key to success at this level isn't signing big-name individuals; it’s having a tight-knit, grounded group of players who fight for each other and leave their egos at the door.

We don't need players who think they belong in the Premier League; we need honest, hard-working characters who buy into his vision. My advice would simply be to protect that team spirit at all costs. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

It might sound like two things, but they are completely linked: I would change the ownership of the stadium so we can install an artificial 3G/4G surface. When the old club was dissolved in 2014, the historic £1-a-year peppercorn rent contract was ripped up, meaning the phoenix club now has to pay a heavy commercial rent, which drains our finances. Our new owner, Ali Al-Hamad, has his heart set on buying the stadium back, and securing the freehold is vital for our long-term survival.

Once we own it, installing an artificial surface would be a game-changer. It’s early days, but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Dorking Wanderers or Torquay United have got to be right up there pushing for promotion, but if I have to pick a definitive winner, I'm backing Marc White’s side.

His attitude is absolutely perfect for this level; he is a unique character who is always relentlessly driving his club forward in his own distinct way. Who’ll be the surprise package? After two seasons fighting for safety, you can't completely ignore Salisbury.

Now that we've established a solid foothold at this level, we have shown we can be incredibly stubborn, well-organised, and tough to beat, especially at home. If we can turn a few of last year's tight draws into wins and add a bit more depth upfront during the summer, we are perfectly capable of ruffling a lot of feathers. But aside from us, watch out for Farnham Town.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Most opposition fans look at our mascot, Chalkie the Panda, and assume he was chosen simply because a panda matches Salisbury's distinct black and white club colours. In fact, his name and identity carry a brilliant double meaning.

First, it’s a direct tribute to club legend and prolific goal scorer Ian Chalk, who was affectionately nicknamed 'Chalkie' during his fantastic playing days for the Whites. Secondly, the panda itself is a nod to a legendary piece of local history. Back in January 1969, a group of university students pulled off a massive rag-week prank by carving a giant, 55-foot panda head directly into the chalk hillsides of Cockey Down in Laverstock, just outside Salisbury.

It became known as 'The Great Laverstock Panda Mystery' and was a beloved part of the landscape before it eventually faded back into the grass. Chalkie the mascot brings both of these great stories together, and who knows, maybe one day the famous panda will finally be re-carved back into the Wiltshire hills for a new generation to see!

article.title: The Fans' View: Why things are looking very different at Slough Town
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
New badge, new manager, a new pitch and a wave of new footballers. It’s all-change at Slough Town this season as it’s out with the old and in with the new at Arbour Park. Alan Julian replaces Aldershot-bound player-boss Scott Davies, and that of course means the Rebels will lose a little bite from their midfield as well.

Things are very different - so will fans get a look at life at the other end of the Enterprise National League South table? Slough super-fan Scott McNeish answers our questions ahead of 2026/27, with kick-off little over a week away. Sum up your club’s summer so far in just three words Rebuilding.

Hungry. Identity. What are your expectations for next season - and are they realistic?

I’m hoping that we can look upwards this season and try to break into the top half of the table and stay there. We were in the bottom half last year and the worry of relegation was too much to handle. With a new manager, a new way of playing and a number of new players I’m hoping they can hit the ground running and surprise a few people.

What ground are you looking forward to visiting? The only new ground for me this season is Cheriton Road, home of Folkestone Invicta. I’m also interested in revisiting Farnham Town as my last visit was over six years ago and it has been transformed since then with a focus on the fans’ matchday experience.

What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in? I’ve got big hopes for Ruben Shakpoke this year. I would like to see him play more regularly which will then mean he can start scoring goals.

Injuries stopped him getting a lot of minutes last season. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? I’d just say to Alan Julian that so long as the team he picks gives us 100 per cent effort and puts the work in and never give up, then the majority of Slough fans will back him and the team to the hilt.

I’d rather the team had a go at trying to win games rather than not to lose them. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? My biggest bug bear is the shallowness of the terracing at each end of the ground.

I would like to see bigger steps to get a better view of the pitch. I’d also like to see some terracing added on the side opposite the main stand so away supporters can get a better view when we have to segregate. Who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

It’s going to be another tight one, but I’ll say Torquay United will finally get over the line. Who’ll be the surprise package? I think Farnham Town are very well equipped to give it a really good go.

Some decent signings, and if they can start well they could be in and around the play-offs. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Dawid Rogalski of Walton & Hersham.

Been firing in goals for a number of seasons so looking forward to see what he can achieve a level up. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Slough Town have lost in the FA Cup second round nine times and have never made it to the third round.

I’m hoping we can break this curse this year - by beating Aldershot Town!

article.title: The Fans' View: Tonbridge Angels' wings are growing
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Tonbridge Angels certainly haven’t looked out of place since entering the competition back in 2019. It’s pretty much progress year-on-year for the Kent club, who continue to be a huge asset to their community after putting down a new pitch the whole areas benefits from. But after six years in the division, fans are wondering if they could now be ready to put together a push for promotion.

After all, we did see plenty of the non-tipped teams having a real go in the Enterprise National League South last season - and one of them even went up! Under 43-year-old manager Alan Dunne, the signs are encouraging, as Angels regular Liz Somerford explains in the latest instalment of our fan season preview. Sum up your club’s summer so far in just three words Surprising, promising, exciting!

What are your expectation for next season - and can they be achieved? I’d like to see a solid start to the season and then push for a play-off spot. Realistically, with our budget and not being full time, I think that is the most we can hope for.

A decent FA Cup run would be fun, too! What ground are you looking forward to visiting? Torquay is always a good weekend away, it’s the week before Christmas this season and I hope we can recreate last year’s result and the afterparty when the chairman and her husband joined us in a Torquay nightclub!

I am also looking forward to a few new grounds for me - Braintree, Billericay and Walton & Hersham. What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in Can I name two? Bunmi Babajide because he grew into a fantastic player under Alan Dunne last season, after many of us fans expected him to be one of the first out of the door when Craig Nelson left.

And Bailey Akehurst, because he is a nice guy, a great player and my personal favourite! You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Stop signing Maidstone players!

No seriously I don’t think I could tell him anything useful, he has really impressed me and I just hope we can hang on to him for a few seasons because he is definitely destined for the higher leagues. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? The ladies’ toilets!

They could definitely do with an upgrade. But honestly I love it there and although there are plans for improvements when finances allow, it’s still a great day and the fans and the food are the best. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

I’m useless at predicting but I’ll guess at Torquay United. Who’ll be the surprise package? Hopefully Tonbridge Angels!

But of the teams coming up I think Folkestone Invicta will be one to watch under ex-Angels manager Jay Saunders. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? I think we are still light of a goalscorer (or two), I wouldn’t mind seeing Nathan Odokonyero back, he impressed on loan a couple of seasons back, and his name makes for a great chant!

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Probably the reason behind the ‘Angels’ part of our name, as we moved from the old Angel Ground on Angel Lane near the Angel pub (which was two minutes walk from the rail station so much kinder to away supporters) many years ago but by then Angels was officially part of our name.

article.title: The Fans' View: 'How my beloved Torquay United can take the next step'
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
Today we kick-off our close season mega mission - speaking to a supporter at every club, getting their views on the season gone, the one ahead and what advice they would give their manager! We’re asking each of the fans the same ten questions as we find out a little more about the past ten months, and what makes their club so special. We begin with a supporter still licking their wounds as Torquay United’s Joseph Pope details the ups and the down of a campaign that ended in heartache as the Gulls lost to Hornchurch in the Enterprise National League South Promotion Final.

He’ll be known to many in the game for his well-read OffTheLine blog that helps bring the game to life in the lower leagues. So what was his favourite moment? What are the early 2026/27 predictions and what rival player would he most like to get his hands on?

Let’s find out. Give us your three-word assessment of your club’s season. Nearly.

Chaotic. Final. What ground did you love visiting the most?

I love Twerton Park. There is something hugely captivating about a game under the lights, at Twerton Park, in that away end, with a strong away following. It is always one of my favourite fixtures of the year, and even though this year's game was arguably our worst, it remains a standout.

One of the big strengths of our club is the fanbase, and it's so rewarding to see so many Torquay United fans in that away end together. Who was your club’s Player of the Season? He got my Player of the Season and he got my Young Player of the Season Vote.

An easy pick: Sonny Blu Lo-Everton. He may not get the goals of Jordan Young or Louis Dennis, but Sonny Blu was by far and away the standout of the season. A tremendous footballer, and one that was at the heart of everything that we did well.

We are a different side without him. In my opinion, he has been THE best performing midfielder in the league this season . What was the single best moment of last season?

The play-off semi-final, our 4-2 win over Dorking Wanderers. We scored four that day, and we really could have scored 14, let alone four! Deon Moore was having a field day leading the line, and should - and could - have got a hattrick.

Jordan Young had one of his "good days" and as has been customary he sprinkled his usual magic with his wand of a left foot with two goals. Not to mention, what an atmosphere! If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be?

Ooh - a great question! It would be between two for me: Harrison Foulkes (Dorking Wanderers) or Charlie Seaman (Ebbsfleet United). Right-back has been a problem position for us all season, and we have tried just about every option in that department - with little success!

For me, Seaman is the best right-back in the league by a country mile. He always scores against us, and I think he should be playing higher. Harrison Foulkes was - in my opinion - the best goalkeeper in the league last year, and he played brilliantly against us.

The pair of them would address some of the areas for improvement on our side. You’ve got two minutes alone with manager Jimmy Ball... what advice would you give him?

Right then, Jimmy - a couple of things. 1) Too many changes from week to week doth butter no parsnips - continuity is key! 2) It is an honour to manage Torquay United - take advantage of the opportunity and give your all.

3) If we ever short on the bench, fill it with a youth player - we have an academy for a reason! 4) The summer recruitment should revolve around pace and power in the wide areas. 5) Ignore the outside noise, and focus on the job at hand - clarity and peace of mind is key!

6) Give Sonny Blu Lo-Everton a new three year deal, lock him away till August, and turn off your phone! What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? In my opinion, we have the best stadium in the league.

That said, I think that we probably harness about 50 per cent of the potential that we can do. We need to modernise the food outlets, and re-develop the corners of the ground to provide a better fan experience. Ideally, we should make the main stand see through perspex lined to allow more line through so the pitch can better recover in adverse weather.

It would be nice if we could have the big screen a) working better and b) utilised more. It’s early days, but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? We sacked a manager that finished second, so we have to be going for the title!

But I think the favourites will be Dagenham & Redbridge. They will - and are - hand-picking signings right from the top shelf. If they don't do it?

I wouldn't bet against Dorking Wanderers. They are determined to get it right, and Marc White means business this year. If Torquay United finishes in the top three, we have done well.

Who’ll be the surprise package? Keep an eye out for Billericay Town. Not many general punters will give them much of a chance, but don't write them off.

They have got one of the best managers in the league in Danny Scopes, and he got Aveley into the National League South play-off, and they have also got one of the best recruiters in non-league in Adam Drew. What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? Our new signing Callum Morton is a lifelong Torquay United fan.

His family are season ticket holders, he regularly watches games at Plainmoor, and used to go to school in the bay. It would be nice to see a Torquay lad take Torquay United back to the National League - you can but hope!

article.title: The Fans' View: Truro City heading back to their happy place!
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
In the end, Truro City’s taste of life in the Enterprise National League may have been short and not so sweet. But that has only increased the determination to get back to the top table and experience it all again. The Tinners will feel they have unfinished business after a short stay after they became the first Cornish club to ever play at that level.

Some tough days won’t be putting them off trying to reclaim their place, despite first-season nerves. Truro have kept faith with those who took them there - and crucially their title-winning manager John Askey will lead the charge again. He has backed his team to learn from last season, and improve as players in the process.

We asked Ian Hyland to give us his rundown and in the latest Fans’ View, he hopes having a similar squad to the one that earned promotion in 2024/25 could work in their favour. Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Quiet so far. Fixture release day is on Friday July 10 - who’s your ideal first day opponent?

A lower placed team at home! Gives the best chance for a first day win. Important to start the season well.

What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season? Torquay United’s Plainmoor - they are the closest team to us geographically… yet still two hours away! A bit of a rivalry has emerged over the last few years What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in Dom Johnson-Fisher.

He can be a real threat this season. His pace is electric. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him?

Be brave with team selections - play on the front foot as much as possible. Staying full-time this season should help with that. What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium?

Some terracing in the flat areas that are not the main stands so people don't have views obstructed by being 3-4 deep. It's a new stadium, so I know it's all still a work in progress. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27?

Obviously, I am going to say Truro, but I know it will be tight, this league always is! The usual five or six teams will be pushing for the top again. Who’ll be the surprise package?

Dagenham & Redbridge or Chelmsford - not really a "surprise" per se, but I expect them both to be challenging much higher up this year than last year given the investment and hype around the clubs. If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Sam Dreyer from Torquay - really impressed with him when we last played Torquay a couple of seasons ago.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? We have arguably the best mascot/mascot name around. It is a Cornish Chough - a county bird - - dressed as a Cornish miner, and it is called Brian Chough.

article.title: Welcome to the Enterprise National League South: Walton & Hersham
article.author: Tom Scott and Richard Dorman
article.html:
Here is the lowdown on Enterprise National League South Walton & Hersham ahead of the new season. Factfile Last Season: Southern League Premier South - Champions Top Scorer: Dawid Rogalski (22) Manager: Kevin James Ground: Elmbridge Xcel Sports Hub Best National League Performance: N/A How they got here... Walton & Hersham's golden era is now more than half a century old – the 1972-73 FA Amateur Cup, won at Wembley without conceding a single goal across the entire competition.

Their manager and several key players promptly decamped to Wimbledon, and the Swans have been trying to recapture those heights ever since. Along the way, the club inadvertently birthed punk band Sham 69 – the name was taken from a piece of graffiti reading ‘Walton & Hersham 69’, a reference to their Athenian League title. A group of university students, claiming to be the ‘youngest owners in world football’, took over a club that had sunk to the tenth tier in 2019.

Four promotions later (and a seven-figure follower count on TikTok), the Swans find themselves in the National League South. The 2025-26 title push survived its biggest test when manager Billy Rowley was lured away to National League Yeovil Town in November with the club already top of the table – his replacement, first-team coach Jakub Pietrzak, kept the machine running without missing a beat. All eyes are now on new man Kevin James who heads into the hot seat for the new season.

A record-breaking FA Trophy run saw the Swans beat three National League sides, including a 4-1 demolition of Sutton United and a 1-0 win against Brackley Town, before fellow Surrey club Woking ended it in the fifth round. The league title was confirmed on Easter Monday, completing a journey from the tenth tier to the sixth in just seven seasons. Keep an eye out for...

As far as Dawid Rogalski goes at in a Walton & Hersham shirt it’s a case of ‘insert superlative here’. The prolific frontman and top scorer was a huge part in their historic title win last season and will relish the chance to show what he can do at a higher level. Main Image - Walton & Hersham FC

article.title: The Fans' View: 'I'm a big supporter while keeping Weston's players fighting fit!'
article.author: Sam Elliott
article.html:
This summer we’ve been asking fans of every club in the three National League divisions for their take on last season - and the one ahead of us. Now we’re changing things up with Weston-super-Mare physio Amy Callow answering our questions. She is a big supporter too, and has taken us behind the scenes with some of her responses and confirmed players are always well fed when they head to the Optima Stadium!

It was a brilliant campaign for the season as the side finished sixth after they enjoyed a club-record run in the FA Cup. Can they have an even better one next time by winning promotion? We’re little over a month from the big kick-off!

Sum up your club’s summer so far in three words Ready to go! Fixture release day is on Friday July 10 - who’s your ideal first day opponent? Hopefully we will be at home and it would be good to get someone we get a great crowd with so Dorking or Dagenham & Redbridge, one of the big boys maybe?

What ground are you looking forward to visiting next season? For me and my job, I love a ground with a large changing room so there's plenty of space to set up a massage couch and not just get shoved in the showers! I think Dagenham was one of the best last year.

What one player would you not want to lose this summer, even if a club record bid came in You can’t ask me that… like picking a favourite child!! I don’t want to lose any of my players. They are the best group I have the pleasure and honour of working with and make me feel like I am a big part of the team.

it's a big family. You’ve got two minutes alone with your club’s manager - what advice would you give him? Be confident.

Don’t second guess and go with your gut. Oh and we need to get an air tag for your car keys and phone….. maybe give me a pay rise too!

What’s the one thing you would change about your team’s stadium? I would love a larger physio room and changing rooms but we have a massive rebuild coming in 2027/28 so everything will be brand spanking new. We have not had a scoreboard for the last 12 months so need one of those but I think that is coming during the next season too.

Although I will miss doing the time checks for our goalkeeper. It’s early days but who’s winning the league in 2026/27? Torquay United.

Who’ll be the surprise package? I am always wrong with this! I think we at Weston always surprise people.

We have had four great seasons and people still write us off each year. Folkestone could surprise a few. They seem on a roll.

If you could sign one player this summer from any team in the division, who would it be? Don’t ever take any notice of other football teams. Would love to have one of our loan players back from last year but I know that’s not going to happen.

What's one thing about your club that opposition fans probably don't know? That Weston offer hot food in the bar after the game for the away players. So many teams in the league now don’t do this.

I find this a real shame after you have travelled for hours, the boys have played hard and then have long trip home. Everyone has food outlets or tea huts. I think one club last year fed their team burgers, pies etc but we were told to walk down the road to the shops!

Luckily it was a warm day and not raining!
